items.title: Anchorage: A City Within the Wild
items.summary:
In  Anchorage , exploring nature isn’t only for a rare free day or a well-planned vacation; it’s a part of daily life, as integral to the city as its infrastructure and cultural offerings. A day here may start with a morning walk on any of the hundreds of miles of trails, continue with freshly caught salmon for lunch at a restaurant with coastal views, and end with a sunset picnic on a rocky outcropping, where the only sounds are crashing waves and the fleeting glimpses of beluga whales.   
  Located on a coastal plain that shifts into alpine slopes farther east, Anchorage is unique
items.text: ' data-toggle="tooltip" title="Link Copied" class="DDPNavbarItem js-social-action-tracked" data-position="Sticky Header" data-service="Link" data-action="Copied" aria-label="Copy Link"> Copy Link Facebook Twitter Reddit Flipboard Pocket Sponsored By Visit Anchorage, Alaska In Anchorage , exploring nature isn’t only for a rare free day or a well-planned vacation; it’s a part of daily life, as integral to the city as its infrastructure and cultural offerings. A day here may start with a morning walk on any of the hundreds of miles of trails, continue with freshly caught salmon for lunch at a restaurant with coastal views, and end with a sunset picnic on a rocky outcropping, where the only sounds are crashing waves and the fleeting glimpses of beluga whales. Located on a coastal plain that shifts into alpine slopes farther east, Anchorage is unique in how its different ecosystems overlap, creating rich diversity in wildlife, botany, and geology. You can experience the best of nature while still enjoying all the creature comforts of urban life and stumble across breathtaking sights without even looking for them. In this guide, we’ve given you some starting points for exploring the wild from Alaska’s biggest city, with wonders ranging from undisturbed wooded trails to marshes that all kinds of animals call home. Ready to take a walk on the wild side? Fishing season runs roughly from late May to early September. Wayde Carroll for Visit Anchorage Ship Creek This 25-mile-long river flows from the Chugach Mountains down into the Port of Alaska on Anchorage’s northern side, where it’s become a popular spot for sport fishing and bird watching. Thanks to its mud and sedge flats, and ocean-fed waters, this area is home to a massive annual run of coho and Chinook salmon. In fact, it’s the only urban Chinook fishery in the world. The 5.8-mile Ship Creek Trail is a perfect way to spend time in nature without leaving the city limits, providing views of salmon spawning and swimming upstream during the summer. Stops along the way, like Ship Creek Overlook Park and the pedestrian bridge just off King’s Landing, provide especially great panoramas of the river and the surrounding mountains. It’s not uncommon to see anglers trying their luck for 20- to 30-pound salmon, and you can even visit the statue of Dena’ina matriarch Grandma Olga , fish filets in her hands and a bronze drying rack behind her. The trail’s namesake is a former Anchorage mayor and Alaska governor. Chris Arend for Visit Anchorage Tony Knowles Coastal Trail For a longer walk, try this 11-mile path that stretches from downtown Anchorage all the way to the Kincaid Park Chalet. However, if you’re looking for a shorter trek, have no fear: The trail is accessible from multiple points in the city, meaning you can hop on or off. You don’t have to explore on foot either, as the trail can be traversed easily by bike and, in the winter, cross-country skis. No matter how you travel the trail, you’re guaranteed some incredible views of downtown Anchorage, Mount McKinley (Denali), Mount Susitna, and Fire Island, especially as you reach the hills near Point Woronzof. The trail offers a rare chance to pass through a number of different biomes, as it winds through marsh, muskeg (acidic, waterlogged peatland), and thick spruce forest. There’s also plenty of wildlife nearby, with moose, in particular, enjoying long walks on the path during the winter. Other animals often spotted include sandhill cranes, ermine, bald eagles, and even beluga whales in Cook Inlet, so don’t forget your camera. Trails rising from the sand dunes and following the bluffs provide some of the best views in Kincaid Park. Paxson Woelber via Flickr CC BY 2.0 Kincaid Park For even more great hiking, visit Kincaid Park, a 1,400-acre green space that was once a Cold War missile base. There’s plenty to do in Kincaid: walk down the 40 miles of cleared trails, practice archery on a designated range, paddle through Little Campbell Lake, or play disc golf on an 18-hole course. There are also seven different soccer fields, a motocross course, and a giant sand dune with stunning views of Cook Inlet and the Kenai Peninsula. In the winter, the park becomes a premier destination for sledding and cross-country skiing, with trails for every skill level. The marsh’s many overlapping habitats make it a hub for all kinds of wildlife. Jody O. Photos for Visit Anchorage Potter Marsh Just 15 minutes south of downtown, this part of the Anchorage Coastal Wildlife Refuge is one of the best wildlife viewing spots in all of Alaska, offering sweeping vistas of the Turnagain Arm tidal waterway and half a mile of boardwalk across the channels and sedges. This wetland ecosystem is full of creatures big and small, from muskrats paddling through the water to the occasional moose taking a dip. And birders, rejoice: The marsh is home to more than 130 bird species, including Arctic tern, Canada geese, trumpeter swans, red-necked grebes, and northern pintails. Pro tip: Visit in April for the greatest variety of migrating birds, or in midsummer to see three different species of salmon schooling under the boardwalk. Information panels and telescopes along the path make it easy to enjoy a self-guided tour and take in the sights and sounds of the marsh at your own pace. You can also see the marsh from aboard the Alaska Railroad or while driving down the Seward Highway . Beluga Point is also a significant archaeological site, with artifacts 8,000 to 10,000 years old. Monica Whitt for Visit Anchorage Beluga Point Also along the Seward Highway sits Beluga Point, a rocky promontory named for the population of beluga whales that can be spotted each July and August when they come to catch salmon in the inlet. However, no matter what time of year you visit, 180-degree views of the Chugach Mountains make this a worthwhile place to stop and take in your surroundings. items.title: The Best Haunted Hotels to Book for a Spooky Getaway
items.summary: Nothing beats staying in a hotel whose suites hold some stories — especially if they’re of the spooky variety. The same friends who roll their eyes at mentions of luxury amenities and amazing views will be wide-eyed when you tell them about the ghost you accidentally ate breakfast with, the wailings you heard on your way to the icebox, or your run-in with an uncanny Victorian woman wearing all black. Booking a room at a regular old hotel will give you a few nice photos and a comfy robe; booking a room at a  haunted  one will give you tales of terror to tell for the rest of your life.

Booking a room at a regular old hotel will give you a few nice photos and a comfy robe; booking a room at a haunted one will give you tales of terror to tell for the rest of your life. At these hotels, lodges, inns, and resorts around the world, the supernatural is embraced and the unsettling is celebrated. Unexplained occurrences are simply part of the experience, and those with a healthy level of morbid curiosity will find no shortage of places to explore. Here, dark lore is hidden in every nook and cranny: a quack doctor’s treatment room, geothermal soaking pools, an old-school saloon, and a clown statue collection. The Marshall House - Savannah, Georgia Savannah has long been known for its thriving ghost population, many of whom have taken up residence at the city’s oldest hotel. Established in 1851 by Mary Magdalene Marshall, the building has played many roles: a makeshift hospital during the mid-19th-century yellow fever epidemic, a Union hospital near the end of the Civil War, and a temporary home to Joel Chandler Harris, creator of Uncle Remus, during the Reconstruction era. It’s no wonder then that guests frequently report odd activity in the hotel’s period-detailed rooms and cozy library. Common occurrences include the sound of children running down the halls at night, strange figures spotted in the foyers, doorknobs rattling, and faucets turning on on their own. Many Savannah ghost tours stop outside the hotel, but nothing beats drinking spirits amongst the spirits during the nightly social hour (sometimes with live entertainment!). items.title: Dorothee Meilichzon
items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu Experimental PORTO INFANTE SAGRES Porto - Portugal opening december 2026 HOTEL MYLOS Corsica Chem. de Paomia Montalbo, 20130 Cargèse, Corsica 2025 Designing a hotel in Corsica is a rare opportunity. Our second stroke of luck was that it was located in Cargèse, a village I knew well, with its two churches, its Bon Accueil bar, its harbour, its magnificent beaches, and its ice cream parlour on the road to Sagone. Building a hotel overlooking the Mediterranean, with panoramic views, is an ambitious and demanding undertaking. Our third stroke of luck was to work with an architectural firm like Orma, which envisioned a building made from earth excavated on site, fragmented and nestled within the maquis. And so it all began: Corsica, the endless sea, the maquis, and the earth. Naturally, it was essential to reconnect with the history of the village, a Greek settlement in Corsica, with its orderly streets, orange-tiled roofs, shifting levels, and breathtaking views. The rooms are mineral and textured. Nothing is smooth. The rock emerges here and there. Desert Modernism thus became a starting point for this thoroughly contemporary project, perched on a mountainside and exposed to the elements. We wanted to tell the story of the Mediterranean, with a few nods to Greek mythology through recreated columns, alcoves, and friezes carved into the plaster. But above all, we wanted to tell the story of Corsica: its shepherds, the colour black, the holm oak, the rock, fishing, and its churches. The colours are matte. Wood is sculpted into waves, fragments of tiles are embedded in the plaster, and tables feature amphora-inspired handles. Friezes depicting waves adorn the bathroom walls, marble is veined with green, lime-washed surfaces take on shades of ecru and beige, wood turns red, concrete is black, and the rock remains raw. The headboards evoke shepherds' hats, the fabrics recall fishing ropes, and the bathrooms draw inspiration from ancient architecture. The sea is everywhere: in every window, from every balcony. It borders the swimming pool, the spa, and the restaurant terrace, perched at the very top of the building, where the most spectacular view unfolds towards infinity, with the rooftops of Cargèse in the distance. The maquis breaks through here and there, crossing the ground to create small inner gardens. A giant belombra tree inhabits the atrium, providing welcome shade. Clients : Pierre Mattei & Dominique Leca Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Photos : Julie Ansiau EXPERIMENTAL CHALET Val d'Isère Rue de la Poste, 73150 Val-d'Isère, Savoie, France Christmas 2024 / Christmas 2025 Located at the foot of the slopes, in the heart of the Val d’Isère ski resort, this expansive hotel sits in a small high-altitude village in the Vanoise mountains and features 113 rooms. It is our largest hotel project to date. It represented a real challenge for us: how could we recreate a contemporary mountain spirit? Almost immediately, this imposing building of slate, concrete and wood brought to mind an American-style lodge. Timber logs, branches, stonework and woodwork would become our starting point. “The spirit of the forest” became our guiding architectural concept, shaping everything from door frames, cupboards, headboards and handles to bathroom furniture and the benches surrounding the imposing stone fireplace. Naturally, we also wanted to pay tribute to skiing. Val d’Isère is a renowned resort, known for its demanding slopes and sporting spirit. We designed mirror frames inspired by ski tips, incorporated snow-white marble, and created table legs from sections of ski poles. Above all, we invented our own “ski” finish: a surface reminiscent of the snow on the famous Face de Bellevarde slope after a day of skiing, marked by long, sweeping tracks sculpted into a lime-based plaster finish. And, of course, we wanted to celebrate Savoy and its traditions. We drew inspiration from traditional Savoyard wooden

items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu BRASS restaurant Paris 131 boulevard Saint-Germain, Paris VI june 2025 « Brass » comme le laiton, qui est bien sûr très présent par touche : encadrements, poignées, pieds de table, habillage muraux … Aussi bien dans le restaurant qu’au niveau de sa façade tout en bois massif et laiton. Mais surtout « Brass », comme les cuivres, hommage à la musique. Nous avons donc dessiné des poignées clefs (musique), des lampes cymbales, des appliques en papier qui rappellent les accordéons, des bas-reliefs en plâtre qui rappelle une lyre, un grand gramophone qui anime le back bar de la salle « plus club » du restaurant, et enfin un piano laqué rouge, quart de queue qui trône à côté de la porte tambour. Enfin « Brass « comme brasserie, mais une brasserie presque à l’américaine : tin ceiling fabriqué à New York, mosaïque en grès à motif géométrique, mobilier sur mesure dessiné pour Brass comme ces grandes banquettes en bois, inspirées de celles des anciennes grandes gares américaines. Et enfin quelques éléments de décor qui nous sont chers, constants dans le travail de Dorothée Meilichzon : miroirs, symétrie, tissus à motifs géométriques et laques brillantes afin de conférer à ce restaurant un esprit convivial et contemporain. Client : Maison Bucher Interior design + furniture : Dorothee Meilichzon Graphics : Violaine & Jeremy Images – @benoitlinero HENRI London Covent garden - London June 2024 For the new HENRI restaurant, with chef Jackson Boxer, we have worked on an interior mixing codes from the traditional british pub, mixed with inspirations for the typical french brasserie : So we have some long banquettes paired with booth seating. Dark wooden wall panelling with some dark greens, lights blues and bordeaux color. Leather mixed with velvet. We have also used some Art Nouveau elements typical from the brasseries : details on the arms of the banquettes, frosted glass globes, Thonet chairs and bespoke organic suspensions. Those botanical shapes also pay tribute to the historical fruits and vegetables market of Covent Garden. Client : Experimental Group Interior design + furniture : Dorothee Meilichzon Chef : Jackson Boxer Graphics : Justine Goutal Images – @wethefoodsnobs SUPERNOVA London 25 Peter St, London octobre 2023 Strong of our partnership with BVC group on Crème Cookie shops in London, Paris, Riad, Bahrain, Dubai and Lyon, we have designed their brand new concept of smash burgers in London, just opened in Covent Garden. Brushed aluminum, granito floor, grooved stainless steel and a luminous ceiling. Client : BVC Group Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Photos : Anton Rodriguez CRÈME Dubaï Crème, 2D St – Al Wasl – Dubai November 2023 COWLEY by Jackson Boxer Cowley, Cheltenham GL53 9NL, Royaume-Uni July 2023 Built In 1695, This Manor Has Changed Hands A Number Of Times Until James Horlick Became The Owner In 1895 Doing Most Of The Alterations Of The Building, Together With Colonel Heber Percy, The Next Owner. This Manor, Now Turned Into An Hotel Also Has Stables, A New Modern Extension, And A Large Spa, Counting 36 Rooms In Total And Numerous Living Rooms : Garden Room, Game Room, A Cocktail Bar, A Cocktail Lounge, A Restaurant, A Library, A Mud Room, Two Swimming Pools … Overall We Wanted To Do What We Love To Do : A Mix Of Geometric Elements, A Mix Of Styles, Of Eras, Celebrating The Multiple Alterations Of The Buildings From 1695 To The 2000s. So At The End A Joyeux Bordel. Our Main Inspiration Was Of Course The Building Itself Mixing Very Classical Inspirations As A Tribute To The Original Manor : Baledaquin Beds, Blurred Maple, Verdigris, Sophisticated Rattan Furniture … Mixed With Contemporary Elements Such As : Enameled Lava, Lime Walls, Very Graphic Fabrics And Carpets, Full Upholstered Furniture, Bold Colors, Glossy Lacquer And A Lot Of …. Checkerboard Patterns ! And This Was A Tribute To Alice In Wonderland : Lewis Carol Has Written His Alice At Cowley Manor Inspired By The Ground

items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu ECC Chinatown - London 13a Gerrard St, London W1D 5PS, UK september 2025 The new ECC Chinatown continues the story we began writing in 2009 : a plush cocktail bar with mirrors and velvet. But above all, it's a place that fits into its context : Gerrard St in London, and therefore a tribute to Chinatown. Dragon scales, bamboo, braiding, shades of purple, brown, and violet. Whether woven into the carpet or on the wall with a 1960s screen, everything recalls the dragon's skin. The furniture is extra soft, covered in fabrics with bronze scales, reinforced with stainless steel. The counters are adorned with bamboo sticks, mirrors, black/purple marble, and woven wood. These details place this party venue in the vibrant nightlife of Soho. Client : Experimental Group Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Photos : Romain Ricard La Compagnie - Paris 7 rue Lobineau, Paris VI septembre 2024 Client : Experimental Group Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Graphic Design : Clovis Retif Photos : Patrick Locqueneux Experimental Cocktail Club - flatiron NEW YORK 6 W 24 St - New York 10010 august 2024 One floor down, we enter the entrails of the place : the cocktail bar. Here, it is no longer with the leaves that we played but with the roots of their trees. Flexible, they descend from the ceiling, wrap around the columns, embrace the globes of the lamps, and structure the walls. Successively in lacquered wood or shiny metal when they invade the counter and its shelves of bottles. A dark, hushed, very warm atmosphere thanks to the large benches covered in Zak+Fox fabrics, the colored glass wall lights by Sophie Lou Jacobsen, as well as large mirrors. This deliberately organic space revisits the codes of Art Nouveau, dear to French bistros and brasseries, but in a more nocturnal vision with amber hues reminiscent of scotch, rye, and rum ! A large white lacquered piano is placed in the middle, for a pianist of course, or a DJ, in a nod to the Experimental Cocktail club in Paris. Client : Experimental Group Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Graphic Design : Clovis Retif Photos : Evan Sung La Compagnie - flatiron - New York La Compagnie - flatiron NEW YORK 6 W 24 St - New York 10010 july 2024 The team wanted to pay tribute to wine, to the land, but also to all the elements and natural events that allow its development : the harvests, the sun, the moon, the earth, the minerals .... We kept from the previous place the brick, typical of New York, as well as the wooden floor, to which we brought more materials, more light: straw, lime, walnut burl, leather, marble, foliage, ceramic, embroidery. The moon orbits both on the fabrics, in imprint on the lime but also in the alabaster which imitates its surface so well. Clovis Retif, a French artist came to draw on the fabrics of the benches, strong symbols of the earth and wine, but also of the city of New York. The marble, leather and bronze counter is divided into three parts, the central part of which becomes a table d'hôtes. Customers thus fully invest the bar and mingle with the teams busy preparing plates, cutting ham and filling glasses. Individual tables with integrated ice buckets, in green marble, bronze and walnut, round tables with rotating tops, communal tables, as well as a large central piece of furniture that showcases the large wine book, in which the answer to the mystery wine of the day is inevitably hidden ! items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu Roissy CDG Aéroport Roissy Charles de Gaulle, Terminal 2G avril 2022 Paris Aéroport nous a appelés en juin 2017 pour réfléchir autour, non pas d’un lounge mais d’une salle d’embarquement ! A Roissy, celle du terminal 2G. Un espace d’attente, où les gens restent, parfois un long moment, où rien n’est à vendre, mais tout à imaginer. Un espace où passent tous les passagers, ceux qui voyagent beaucoup autant que ceux qui prennent l’avion pour la première fois. Un espace sur lequel aucun architecte d’intérieur ne s’était récemment vraiment penché. 1300m2 d’expériences à inventer, de mobiliers à dessiner, d’ennui à tromper, de convivialité à créer, d’intimité à préserver. En quelques mots théâtraliser la salle d’embarquement tout en gardant le passager informé. Notre approche a été assez immédiatement de s’approprier le mantra « PARIS vous aime » et de tisser un lien avec la capitale et la France, ses grandes époques de design, son histoire. Le mobilier étant l’élément phare de ce projet - puisque nous ne pouvions toucher la coque - nous avons décidé de célébrer le mobilier des Arts décoratifs. A la fois nos grands savoir-faire (tapissier, serrurier, ébéniste, staffeur, peintre décoratifs... ) mais aussi surprendre le passager avec un mobilier pluriel inspiré des mobiliers des années 1960/70 : ludique, circulaire, articulé, dos à dos, face à face, individuel, collectifs .... autant de scènes de vie que nous avons imaginées en préservant l’intimité grâce à des claustras et totems qui à la manière de vases géants, viennent architecturer les espaces. Nous avons dessiné le mobilier bien sûr mais aussi une immense fresque, au dessus dès fenêtres qui donnent sur le tarmac, inspirée de Sonia Delaunay et qui reprend la vue du ciel des pistes de décollage et d’atterrissage. Nous avons aussi pu pour la première fois à Roissy installer des pièces de mobiliers anciens achetés aux puces de St Ouen : appliques géantes de l’Enac, brises soleil en aluminium, suspensions turbine ! Aussi nous voulions créer des clins d’œil aux monuments parisiens et implanter dans notre scénographie des icônes de l’architecture parisienne : la fontaine du jardin du Luxembourg et ses fameuses chaises, les arches et arcs de Paris ainsi qu’un mobilier urbain créé in situ par les Simonnet. Enfin il nous paraissait essentiel de créer un lien avec l’avion et son imaginaire : aluminium, moquette, fauteuils inclinables et tissu à motifs. La salle d’embarquement devient une transition douce entre le Paris que l’on quitte et l’avion qui va décoller Client : Groupe ADP Interior Architecture + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon Sculpture : les Simonnet Curator : Gilbert Kann Photos : Karel Balas prev / next Back to AIRPORT 26 Roissy CDG --> Summary Block This block is invalid. items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu ACQUA DI PARMA Le Bon Marché Le Bon Marché Rue de Sèvres, Paris VI In 2025, we had the opportunity to design the new Acqua di Parma store within the beauty department at Le Bon Marché in Paris. We incorporated the signature design elements we had previously established for the brand—matte wood, glossy Acqua di Parma yellow lacquer, white lacquer, and varnished latticework — blending them with nods to lemon motifs and arches. These shapes, so central to Acqua di Parma’s identity, were showcased in a setting that pays tribute to Le Bon Marché itself. We sought to celebrate Art Deco style and Le Bon Marché’s iconic staircase through a large, highly geometric wooden feature wall. This design offers a glimpse into a bright, glossy-yellow space at the rear, housing the checkout area and a "bath & body" unit created as a tribute to 1920s furniture. Clients : LVMH Architecture d’intérieur + Design : Dorothee Meilichzon ACQUA DI PARMA Paris 205 rue Saint Honré, Paris I April 2025 Located rue Saint Honoré in Paris, opening right after our boutique in Saint-Tropez, we wanted to pay tribute to Paris of course and to the emblematic perfume bottle of Acqua di Parma. Art deco is the meeting point of the two. We have paid tribute to Jean-Michel Frank on walls with a geometric pattern carved in the marmorino. We have played with arches as they are very strong in Paris but also in Acqua di Parma history. We have created some wooden columns made with the iconic bottle, but also some large steles with the bottle enlarged and turned into a parchment lamp. And as the golden fruits are also the heroes, we have created this table all handmade in enameled ceramic in France in three dimensions with half lemon sculpted. The floor is terracotta mixed with traditional parisian wooden floor, and the warm yellow of Acqua di Parma appears inside the wooden furniture, very bright, very glossy so that some of the south of Italy arrives in Paris. ACQUA DI PARMA Guangzhou november 2024 The boutique in Guangzhou is our first project in China. And as for the other boutiques, we wanted to mix some of Acqua di Parma essentials : the golden fruits, the Art Deco, the arches, the beautiful warm yellow and the symmetry, with some local Chinese inspirations. So we have created, especially for the Guangzhou boutique, some lamps, vases, and murals. The hanging lamps are inspired by traditional Chinese paper lanterns, but in a very recognisable lemon shape mixed with yellow ribbons and pompoms. And as the yellow handmade hat boxes are very important in the Acqua di Parma heritage, we have created some Ming inspired boxes, that are part of the decor, and a subtle tribute to the amazing traditional chinese vases. Also we have created some porcelain vases, blue and white, using some of the patterns we have designed for Acqua di Parma Blue Mediterraneo. The floor is in terracotta, with a chinese grey stone border. The bath and body furniture is inspired by the traditional chinese medicine cabinets, so some white lacquered drawers with at the center a large shelving area with a sink, our arch mirror all in a very dark red glossy lacquer. Finally we have created those huge square arches, in glossy yellow and the entrance of the boutique and in wood inside the boutique. They celebrate the traditional arches but in a very modern way. Client : Acqua di Parma Interior Design + furniture : Dorothee Meilichzon ACQUA DI PARMA Saint-Tropez Place des Lices, Saint-Tropez june 2024 Invade the Place des Lices with the golden fruits of Acqua di Parma! They slip between the furniture, under the shelves and grow bigger until they even become a completely round architecture in order to present Acqua di Parma's summer collection. A solar space with terracotta floors reminiscent of the orange-pink of St Tropez, lime walls, a lacquered ceiling and two large benches that brush against a citrus zest table. Candles, perfumes, diffusers are installed in minimal stainless steel

items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu DIX HECTARES june 2025 Design of an innovative packaging line for Dix Hectares. A new innovative cosmetic brand produced in Montrose, France. The objects are lightweight, with partially recycled glass, a bio-sourced Sulapac lid with a marbled effect, and refillable capsules made from bioresin : flax, hemp, and reed fibers. Client : Charlotte Bouygues Packaging design : Dorothee Meilichzon Graphics : Violaine & Jeremy CHAPEAU Acqua di Parma May 2024 We have designed "Chapeau" for Acqua di Parma, a huge candle in ceramic, handmade in France. Inspired by the shape of the emblematic Art Deco perfume bottle of Acqua di Parma, we have created this two parts candles, that celebrates the joy and vibrance of Acqua di Parma. Client : Acqua di Parma Design : Dorothee Meilichzon MAISON BULLE Vexin, France 2022 " The egg-shaped construction is one of the principles within nature : fruits, air bubbles, biological organs. The angle is an invention of man to satisfy certain techniques. Nowadays, the technique takes a step back from the abstract mathematical conception, and by approaching the forms of organic life, it must serve man in a more direct way », Jean Benjamin Maneval. Jean-Benjamin Maneval (1923-1986), French architect and urban planner, made the first sketches of his six-shell bubble house in 1963 : a little revolution in the field of prefabricated housing and foundation- less architecture. Produced between 1968 and 1970, this house, which has a surface area of 36m2, is formed by assembling six independent reinforced polyester shells. Originally, the architect had imagined these bubble houses as secondary residences with an ergonomic design for a family of four, where the space in each alcove would be optimized to the maximum. In 2014, a non-conformist collector acquired at an auction an authentic 1968 bubble house by Jean-Benjamin Maneval. It is installed on his family estate, a former stud farm in the heart of the Véxin area, for which he has given the artistic direction to KIF, an interdisciplinary creative studio formed by Guillaume Furet and Mélissa Louis. KIF's vision for the redesign of this bubble was that of a capsule of conviviality, a bubble of comfort in the middle of nature, based on a hotel suite : « To bring this vision to life, we wanted the signature of a contemporary designer. The collaboration with Dorothée Meilichzon was an obvious choice, so that she could superimpose her own unique vision and bring a whole new functionality to this singular architectural object. » The bubble house had been designed empty by Maneval, so everything had to be imagined. Dorothée Meilichzon, head of the CHZON studio, which specialises in the design of hotels, bars and restaurants, designed the interior architecture of this house as a hotel suite, in the continuity of JB Maneval's work : no straight lines. A suite set in nature, where you can sleep, read, wash yourself, or invite a few friends for a drink or a dinner, while enjoying the furtive appearance of wild boars and deers through the large plexiglass openings. Each piece of furniture, taking up the double curve of the hull, was designed and manufactured specifi- cally for this project. Five of the shells share a large orange carpet, but each hull has its own function: the "bed" shell, is upholstered in a very graphic Edinburgh Weavers fabric as a nod to the owner of this bubble who is a passionate collector of Vasarely. The "bar" shell is made of Tibor fabric and custom-made furniture in stainless steel. The "entrance" shell hosts a lamp by Axel Chay, facing the view, and is next to a very contemplative "living room" shell furnished with two rounded benches, upholstered in carpet and a Chimera lamp by Vico Magistratti. The "shower" shell, all in Arabescato marble and pastille mosaic, is as white as the house. items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu HOTEL MYLOS Corsica Chem. de Paomia Montalbo, 20130 Cargèse, Corsica 2025 Designing a hotel in Corsica is a rare opportunity. Our second stroke of luck was that it was located in Cargèse, a village I knew well, with its two churches, its Bon Accueil bar, its harbour, its magnificent beaches, and its ice cream parlour on the road to Sagone. Building a hotel overlooking the Mediterranean, with panoramic views, is an ambitious and demanding undertaking. Our third stroke of luck was to work with an architectural firm like Orma, which envisioned a building made from earth excavated on site, fragmented and nestled within the maquis. And so it all began: Corsica, the endless sea, the maquis, and the earth. Naturally, it was essential to reconnect with the history of the village, a Greek settlement in Corsica, with its orderly streets, orange-tiled roofs, shifting levels, and breathtaking views. The rooms are mineral and textured. Nothing is smooth. The rock emerges here and there. Desert Modernism thus became a starting point for this thoroughly contemporary project, perched on a mountainside and exposed to the elements. We wanted to tell the story of the Mediterranean, with a few nods to Greek mythology through recreated columns, alcoves, and friezes carved into the plaster. But above all, we wanted to tell the story of Corsica: its shepherds, the colour black, the holm oak, the rock, fishing, and its churches. The colours are matte. Wood is sculpted into waves, fragments of tiles are embedded in the plaster, and tables feature amphora-inspired handles. Friezes depicting waves adorn the bathroom walls, marble is veined with green, lime-washed surfaces take on shades of ecru and beige, wood turns red, concrete is black, and the rock remains raw. The headboards evoke shepherds' hats, the fabrics recall fishing ropes, and the bathrooms draw inspiration from ancient architecture. The sea is everywhere: in every window, from every balcony. It borders the swimming pool, the spa, and the restaurant terrace, perched at the very top of the building, where the most spectacular view unfolds towards infinity, with the rooftops of Cargèse in the distance. The maquis breaks through here and there, crossing the ground to create small inner gardens. A giant belombra tree inhabits the atrium, providing welcome shade. items.text: Dorothee Meilichzon Menu EXPERIMENTAL CHALET Val d'Isère Rue de la Poste, 73150 Val-d'Isère, Savoie, France Christmas 2024 / Christmas 2025 Located at the foot of the slopes, in the heart of the Val d’Isère ski resort, this expansive hotel sits in a small high-altitude village in the Vanoise mountains and features 113 rooms. It is our largest hotel project to date. It represented a real challenge for us: how could we recreate a contemporary mountain spirit? Almost immediately, this imposing building of slate, concrete and wood brought to mind an American-style lodge. Timber logs, branches, stonework and woodwork would become our starting point. “The spirit of the forest” became our guiding architectural concept, shaping everything from door frames, cupboards, headboards and handles to bathroom furniture and the benches surrounding the imposing stone fireplace. Naturally, we also wanted to pay tribute to skiing. Val d’Isère is a renowned resort, known for its demanding slopes and sporting spirit. We designed mirror frames inspired by ski tips, incorporated snow-white marble, and created table legs from sections of ski poles. Above all, we invented our own “ski” finish: a surface reminiscent of the snow on the famous Face de Bellevarde slope after a day of skiing, marked by long, sweeping tracks sculpted into a lime-based plaster finish. And, of course, we wanted to celebrate Savoy and its traditions. We drew inspiration from traditional Savoyard wooden chests, passed down from father to son, as well as from the carved wooden stamps once used to mark loaves of bread before they were taken to the communal wood-fired oven in the village below the resort. items.title: EATON SQUARE, LONDON - DIMORESTUDIO
items.text: EATON SQUARE, LONDON - DIMORESTUDIO DIMORE STUDIO EATON SQUARE, LONDON Dimorestudio presents a unique reinterpretation of a classic apartment in the heart of Eaton Square, one of London’s most exclusive addresses. The project combines British elegance with a sophisticated, cinematic Italian aesthetic. The apartment, located in a listed historic building and spanning approximately 400 m², has been transformed from a traditional space into an environment rich in atmosphere and visual layers. Each room features custom furnishings, vintage lighting, and Murano glass artworks, creating a harmonious dialogue between history and contemporary design. Dimorestudio approached the apartment as a sophisticated set, drawing inspiration from Italian cultural and cinematic references. The design blends Dimoremilano’s bespoke pieces with iconic mid‑century furniture, rare lighting, and decorative objects sourced from diverse artistic traditions. The deep color palette and carefully orchestrated lighting emphasize the emotional quality of the spaces, evoking a distinctive “Italian magic” through textures, reflections, and contrasts. The result is a residence that goes beyond conventional interior design, becoming an immersive experience where past and present converge in a coherent and captivating visual narrative. ph. items.title: MILANO INDIPENDENZA - DIMORESTUDIO
items.text: MILANO INDIPENDENZA - DIMORESTUDIO DIMORE STUDIO MILANO INDIPENDENZA Emiliano Salci, co-founder of Dimorestudio, unveils his new private apartment in Milan, a space where discretion meets refined contemporary sensibility. The residence is a personal manifesto, balancing warmth with clarity, and intimacy with openness, creating a home that feels welcoming and considered. The apartment unfolds through a fluid sequence of open-living spaces. A long entrance corridor—more reminiscent of a salon than a hallway—introduces interconnected living areas where each space communicates visually and materially with the next. Two secluded bedrooms offer private retreats, completing a layout that harmonizes function, proportion, and atmosphere. The entrance corridor is furnished with symmetrical 19th-century sofas and a row of 1970s lamps by Kazuhide Takahama, establishing a sense of thoughtful layering and subtle eccentricity. Light filters naturally through generously sized windows, highlighting textures, materials, and carefully curated objects throughout the space. Dimorestudio’s signature approach is evident in the eclectic layering of references, periods, and cultures. Antique neoclassical pieces coexist with mid-century modern furniture by designers such as Gio Ponti, Piero Portaluppi, Carlo Mollino, and Osvaldo Borsani. Turkish and Berber rugs, natural textiles, and sculptural lighting fixtures punctuate the rooms, creating a dialogue between heritage and contemporary practice. In the living and dining areas, glossy aubergine walls contrast with furniture and textiles, while ceramics, vases, and art pieces add narrative depth. The bedrooms are quieter and more intimate, featuring warm camel-rose tones, natural fabrics, bespoke bedding, and soft, ambient lighting. Every detail—from furniture placement to tactile surfaces—creates a calm environment, offering comfort and a sensorially rich experience. This apartment is more than a residence: it is a narrative in space, an interplay of light, texture, and history. It demonstrates Dimorestudio’s philosophy: layering over minimalism, warmth over austerity, history integrated with modernity. Emiliano Salci’s new Milan apartment exemplifies a space where function, materiality, and narrative coexist, offering a personal yet universally inspiring approach to living. ph. items.text: étage 5, Latitude 43, St. Tropez - DIMORESTUDIO DIMORE STUDIO étage 5, Latitude 43, St. Tropez Within Latitude 43 , the iconic 1930s building by Georges-Henri Pingusson, a 120-square-meter apartment has been reimagined as a refined tribute to the Modern Movement and nautical aesthetics. Overlooking the Mediterranean, the residence blends rationalist architecture with contemporary design, preserving its historical essence while introducing a sophisticated new language. Bauhaus influences and Gio Ponti references emerge in the interplay of materials and colors—coral Vietri tiles, navy blue walls, and custom-designed furniture crafted from wood and natural fabrics. A curated selection of 20th-century design icons, from Gabriella Crespi to Le Corbusier, coexists with Dimoremilano pieces and decorative objects that narrate stories of life and travel. Every element is meticulously placed, reflecting a cinematic interplay of history, design, and emotion. Ph. items.title: CHLEO - Islyn
items.text: CHLEO - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE The remnants of a fire’s past leaves a mark on human experience. Charred ash and the single plume of smoke from a cooling flame indicate the presence of a gathering, a fleeting moment in time. The physicality of fire helps to tell our stories and was the inspiration behind the design for Chleo; a wine bar in Kingston, NY. CHLEO UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Kingston, NY ROLE Interior Design YEAR 2023 partners Hope and Charles Matthews SELECTED PRESS Inspired by fire, wine, and nourishment – the first things that brought people together – Chleo boils hospitality down to its roots, offering unparalleled service and a second home for a growing neighborhood. Aiming to shift the status quo and create a more equitable and sustainable future, the client’s objective for their first self-owned restaurant in Kingston, NY was to offer the experience of fine dining while stripping away the formality, structure, and elitism that makes it hard to reach. Their mission extended in celebrating the bounty and people of the Hudson Valley, in an effort to connect with the land and those who cultivate it. To support this, we sought to create a space that fosters genuine human connections and memorable experiences with a giving spirit. The restaurant is meant to serve as a diplomatic space for people to reconnect and appreciate the simple joys of a beautiful meal; a respite that pulls cues from Hudson Valley’s life-giving environs and traditions of craftsmanship. For the interior design visioning, we went back to where we started – the hearth – which has long stood as the cornerstone of a home, fostering togetherness. With meticulously considered design, we transformed a forlorn space into moments of discovery through the story of fire. A dark open kitchen against a pale grey limewash nods to the nuanced idea of charred ash and plumes of smoke from a cooling flame – the presence of gatherings past. Carefully placed mirrors animate the energy and flame of the kitchen, no matter where you’re sitting. Foraged and dried seasonal ingredients hang on display and find their way on your plate, offering an intimate connection to the pleasures of Hudson Valley bounty. Hand-carved wood detailing proudly displays the irregularities of spalted maple harvested less than 100 miles away. Every detail of the space is meant to draw you in, create conversation, and provide an experience that could only exist on that particular corner of Kingston. Beyond aesthetics, we were inspired by the chef’s unrelenting commitment to honest sustainability, and saw an opportunity to usher in a new and better era at a human scale. The project bears regional materials and products to form a hyper-localized space; by sourcing through local means, we not only created a space full of nostalgic materials and familiar forms, but worked to amplify the voices of Hudson Valley’s artists, florists, and makers to create a unique sense of renewability within the community. Chleo is a testament to collaboration, conversation, and discovery; an idiosyncratic vessel for expression and innovation, made by and for the locals. Anticipating the needs of a modern era, the spirit of the restaurant believes that a brightly prepared meal and the place with which you enjoy it go far beyond the visual or the taste. It’s something you can feel. PREVIOUS PROJECT NEXT PROJECT

items.title: UCHI D.C. - Islyn
items.text: UCHI D.C. - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE UCHI D.C. UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Washington, D.C. ROLE Interior Design YEAR 2026 partners Hai Hospitality Zebra Barson Procurement Shawmut Design and Construction Reveal Design Group SELECTED PRESS Situated at 1700 M Street NW, just steps from Farragut Square and within walking distance of Dupont Circle, Uchi Washington, D.C. is deeply informed by the character of its surroundings. The Golden Triangle is a lively, walkable neighborhood where cultural institutions, restaurants, residences, and workplaces overlap, creating a steady, day-to-night rhythm. Rather than stand apart, the restaurant is designed to feel embedded within this fabric. Its architecture and interiors respond to the scale, pace, and refinement of the neighborhood, offering a welcoming retreat that feels residential in spirit while remaining quietly transportive. Housed within the ground floor of a newly constructed, sustainability-focused office building, Uchi brings warmth and intimacy to the streetscape, contributing to the neighborhood’s evolving dining culture. The dining experience is conceived as a carefully orchestrated journey, one that unfolds slowly and rewards curiosity. Inspired by New Formalist Modernism and the expressive geometry of mid-century architecture, the space balances structure with softness, precision with emotion. Geometric cutouts, layered thresholds, and fluid circulation create moments of pause and revelation, guiding guests through a sequence of intimate and atmospheric settings. A rich, cinematic palette of crimson, jade green, and muted gold tones sets a sensual backdrop, enhanced by low, flattering light and tactile materials. References to classic film and dreamlike interiors lend the restaurant a sense of romance and mystery, creating an environment that feels both transportive and deeply personal. Throughout the space, subtle moments of concealment and surprise invite exploration. Private dining rooms, softly obscured pathways, and tucked-away corners emerge gradually, fostering a sense of closeness and discovery that mirrors the progression of the meal itself. The result is a restaurant that feels found rather than announced, intimate and immersive, as though it has always belonged there. True to the Uchi philosophy, the design supports an experience defined by warmth, generosity, and human connection. items.title: THE MERCANTILE - Islyn
items.text: THE MERCANTILE - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE The Mercantile is the heartbeat of Sawmill Market, an artisanal food hall in Albuquerque. Inspired by a uniquely New Mexican ethos of open-armed hospitality — and the kitchens, pantries and living rooms that it’s borne from — The Mercantile is a testament to the abundant natural splendors and culinary prowess in The Land of Enchantment. THE MERCANTILE UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Albuquerque, NM ROLE Interior Design Brand Identity YEAR 2020 partners Client: Heritage Hotels F&B Consultants: JLG Hospitality Architect: API Plus Photography: Read Mckendree SELECTED PRESS Built from the bones of a former lumber yard, The Mercantile is Islyn Studio’s modern interpretation of the stocked pantries of New Mexican luminaries. In conjuring the design, the Brooklyn-based studio conducted folkloric and historic research, divining the history of the structure, the psychogeography of the terrain and the real lived experience of Albuquerqueans. Inspired by the New Mexican houses of Georgia O’Keeffe, Islyn envisioned The Mercantile as the Albuquerque kitchen of a fictional long-lost aunt with impeccable taste, whose house always smells of baked bread and who collects wild herbs and dries them from the rafters. The open-air space thrums with the breezy spirit of the American Southwest: its soft, muted colors, lasting natural materials, beams of golden light and waxy cacti greenery. Divided into three distinct areas through the use of half-walls and intentional shelving, The Mercantile offers a full-service culinary experience with retail, cooking and dining on offer. The Pantry is the hearth of the space, teeming with warmth. A wood-burning oven is constantly aglow, with chefs practicing traditional and rustic cooking techniques. Using materials that speak to regional New Mexican craft alongside found vintage pieces, the Wine Bar is designed as an invitation and inspiration, a transition from the outside world into the deeper heart of Sawmill Market. Offering local natural wines as well as a rotating list of selections from around the world, the bar is a natural confluence of guests and locals. The wood detailing around the bar is inspired by the intricate patterns of Navajo basket-weaving. Handmade clay tiles lay the foundation for the space and floor-to-ceiling wooden shelves showcase local art and wild-foraged ephemera — dried white sage picked from highway medians, sun-bleached sticks from mountain walks and dark green jade from Mama’s Minerals across the street, alongside Hansellmann’s pottery vases and a curated selection of provisions, botanicals and handicrafts. The confluence of organic materials and products helps tell the nuanced story of New Mexico’s abundant natural resources and offerings, eschewing the typical retail environment for something down-to-Earth, welcoming and human. The Cafe functions as an intimate eating nook in a friend’s kitchen, inspiring organic conversation and natural collaboration. A humble and relaxed environment, The Cafe offers a rotating, seasonal menu of small, nourishing plates from nearby farms — one of the few, true “farm-to-table” restaurants in the city — served on mid-century style tables and chairs hand-built from dark wood. The Wine Bar, Pantry and Cafe are three manifestations of a new culinary imagination in Albuquerque, a city that still relies heavily on processed foods and conventional produce. By emphasizing the handmade, the seasonal and the locally-foraged, The Mercantile is meant to inspire guests and locals about new ways of living that connect them to place and local culture. items.title: WEST - Islyn
items.text: WEST - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE In the dusty town of Albuquerque, New Mexico, is a bespoke craft cocktail bar that was created for and by the community. WEST UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Albuquerque, New Mexico ROLE Interior Design Branding Identity YEAR 2019 - Opening Soon partners Client: Heritage Hotels F&B Consultants: JLG Hospitality Architect: API Plus Images: 3DQ CG Photography SELECTED PRESS In the dusty town of Albuquerque, New Mexico, hidden in the Sawmill Market is a bespoke craft cocktail bar that was created for and by the community. We spent weeks exploring the red crags of New Mexico — its people, its art, its colors, woods and the unique smoky flavors of the local Piñon. We met ranchers, activists and carpenters. We collected rocks, feathers and ancient arrowheads. And we discovered Vera McGinnis, a local Albuquerque legend who was a rodeo queen and a renegade, the first woman to ever wear pants during performances. In an effort to blur the lines between old and new, masculine and feminine, the West cocktail bar became a monument to Vera, with fringed menus, cut crystal glasses, strings of lights (a nod to her pearls) and leather embossing reminiscent of her horse’s saddle. We paired blush accents with rough textures, soft music juxtaposed against the sharp scent of oak barrel-aged whiskey. These complexities painted a full picture of Vera whose sharp rebellion re-imagined the art of rodeo When people talk about Vera, they tell the story of her last known sighting — riding off into the fuschia sunset of the Sandia Mountain on her horse. We utilized subtle touches of “sunset” in our design in a nod to Vera, and made sure all windows oriented West. Our approach here was to inspire new experiences of intrepid adventure by waving the flags of those who’ve come before. PREVIOUS PROJECT NEXT PROJECT

items.title: THE MANCHESTER - Islyn
items.text: THE MANCHESTER - Islyn Projects All Projects Interior Design Branding In Development About Press & Awards Journal Contact Islyn Studio New York, NY Instagram Follow Us @islynstudio #islynstudio VIEW RECENT PROJECTS CLOSE The Manchester is a lively hotel in Lexington's historic distillery district. Described as "the first high-end hotel in the horse and bourbon capital of the world," The Manchester sits on the site of the historic Ashland Distillery – the city's first registered bourbon producer, which was established in 1865. THE MANCHESTER UCHIKO MIAMI INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE THE TUSK BAR & BRASS INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE NOW NOW HOTEL INTERIOR DESIGN READ MORE LOCATION Lexington, KY ROLE Brand Identity YEAR 2022-2023 partners New Circle The Manchester SELECTED PRESS If the hotel’s restaurant, Granddam , can be considered the esteemed grandmother of The Manchester , our hotel concept envisions the hotel as her spirited grandson. Brimming with youthfulness, a global outlook, and a touch of playfulness, he exudes an expressive and vibrant demeanor. He embraces a colorful wardrobe and possesses a penchant for lively conversations, novel experiences and forging connections with ease. With an audacious spirit at its core, we draw inspiration from manufacturing and industry, incorporating wood block-inspired typography that exudes a sense of solidity. Additionally, our architectural influences shine through as we pay homage to brickwork in our brand icon. When crafting our graphic system, we sought inspiration from Garrett Morgan, the inventive mind from Kentucky, and reimagined his traffic light designs. In our typographic details, we juxtapose the boldness of the type by incorporating IMB Plex mono, a subtle reference to the IBM factory located in Lexington back in 1956, renowned for producing the firm’s first electric typewriter. Overall, our identity purposefully creates a contrast to the interior design, utilizing vibrant splashes of color, strong graphic treatments, and a contemporary flair, all while remaining rooted in rich historical heritage. The Manchester opened in May, 2023. PREVIOUS PROJECT NEXT PROJECT

items.text: Timeline | Yabu Pushelberg Design Studio History Serendipity Studio Close Play Video Serendipity Studio Close "Unbridled energy. Unbridled energy and incredible dreaming of what we wanted to do." glenn "So that’s how it happened. And we kept our separate businesses. It was Glenn Pushelberg Design Associates, and George Design. And we were working under the same roof and same space, different phone numbers, different logo, different entities. And we ended up helping each other with deadlines and cramming. And that’s how we sorted our styles, our sensibility of design linked our drawings, our drawing cells. This is before AutoCAD. We would do perspectives with pencil and graphite. I’d begin on one side and he’d begin on the other, working the perspective with shade and shadow. When our pencil lines met, you couldn’t tell the drawing had been created by two different people." george philanthropy to hold Close in service industry Close Heading A variety of devices - irony, scale, metaphor, material use - result ina diverse collection of pieces bound together by a single verb, one that is simultaneously elusive and concrete. Club Monaco distinguished itself through its lifestyle-oriented retail environments, such as incorporating cafés and unique store designs that fostered a sense of community and discovery. When we started Club Monaco. Joe, the founder was inspired by Muji, which at the time was also a young brand from Japan focused on creating basics. I remember our first meeting: he took a square piece of brown kraft paper and said, ‘This is the concept basic.’ We were all thinking, Okay… what exactly do you mean by that? But from the beginning it really was about materiality and about collaborating with artists, which is something we still do today. We did these big murals of the Monaco Casino as storefronts and stuff, and it had humor to it and a lightness to it. And there was an area called The Beaches in Toronto. We did a store there and it was the Monaco Casino but with sand around and stuff. But there was humor to it. It was a different. It was a sand castle iteration of the palace in Monaco." George "There is a humbleness in the imperfect perfectness of things. The humble materials and how they were worked with in a way transformed it into something of ultimate perfection. Make the most out of it, solving problems. I think high humble came from the moment we became a company. From the start, it was all about space, mood, and emotion. We refined that over time, focusing more on scale, proportion, and the emotional resonance we want users to feel in our spaces, rather than the artifice of what they see. That’s our point of difference as a company." glenn club monaco toronto Studio 55 Close Studio 55 Close The From the Cinema of Famous Players' Empress Theatre to the stage of the Princess of Wales Theatre to the after part at Tonic Nightclub, the studio demonstrated talent at staging experience as much as manipulating materials. Aman Residences Tokyo Tokyo | Branded Residences A match made for the heavens Pairing Mori with Aman for their first branded residences Project Details date 2023 Services Art Advisory Styling Interiors Custom Product Design Client Mori Development Brand Aman Region Asia Typology Branded Residences Architect Pelli Clarke & Partners Novel Notoriety ‍ Mori needed a novel idea to set this project apart from others, including the two additional towers it was developing within the same eight hectare district. At the same time, the team required something with established brand presence and status to support a premium. Elevated yet Grounded ‍ Our client sought a literal and figurative crown for Mori JP Tower, the tallest building in Japan. With an emphasis on connectivity, culture, and nature, the upper level residences needed to stay linked to the people and surroundings of the new village below. Partner Pairing ‍ We proposed that Mori collaborate with Aman to launch their first branded residences. Leveraging the Aman's prestige and status to create market attention, while the exclusivity of the inaugural residential offering would captivate the real estate market. Sea to Sky Storytelling ‍ “The design of Aman Residences, Tokyo is an exploration of the relationship between the land, sea, and sky. These elements work in harmony to convey the Aman lifestyle and the design sensibilities of Japan. Nature plays a key role in Japanese culture, and we felt the most honest way of communicating the intention behind the Aman Residences, Tokyo was by honoring that.” ‍ — Glenn Pushelberg The Connection Connected ‍ The residences sold out, with the penthouse reaching the highest recorded value for a Japanese residential property at one hundred forty million dollars, far surpassing its guide price of fifty million dollars. The project also received Interior Design magazine’s Best of Year Award. Drag Click to play "Traditional Japanese spatial concepts are reinterpreted through contemporary materials and technologies, while Western notions of comfort are refined through Japanese principles of restraint. The result is neither strictly Japanese nor Western, but rather a new vocabulary of luxury that speaks to global sensibilities while remaining grounded in local context." items.title: Thoughtful Hotel Concepts & Designs | Lore Group
items.text: Lore Group Design Thoughtful design and interesting use of space is at the heart of everything we do. Our in house design team, led by Creative Director Jacu Strauss, are inspired by our buildings, their history and the neighbourhoods in which they are located. Thoughtful Design There is nothing standard about what we do. Our hotels are as different as the cities and neighbourhoods in which they are located, and their storied designs takes their cue from their unique sense of place. We think about every detail. For us, good design is not about stamping our own “look” on every project; instead, it’s about breathing new life into a building and creating spaces that work. Jacu Strauss Jacu Strauss is the Creative Director of Lore Group. Throughout the design process Jacu places emphasis on exploration and experimentation as a means to showcase the beauty and characteristics of each project and its context, uncovering the stories that bring to life the destination in which each property sits. In concepting and designing both Pulitzer Amsterdam and Riggs Washington DC, Jacu relocated to each destination in order to live and breathe them, ensuring that the properties reflect the communities around them. Caitriona O'Sullivan As Design Director, Caitriona leads the design on all aspects of the properties that a guest sees or touches during their stay, from furniture, fixings and accessories to large construction projects. Caitriona also manages and leads the design team and studio projects. Working closely with Creative Director Jacu Strauss, they approach each project with the aim of showcasing the beauty and potential of each space. Storytelling is at the heart of Lore Group’s narrative, focusing on designs that are not trend based and are authentic to each location. Through design, Caitriona and her team bring each property to life. Whether you'd like to join our design team, ask them a question or have a product you think they'd like, you can contact them below. SAY HELLO

items.title: The Surrey, New York — MBDS
items.text: NEW YORK The Surrey Echoing the heritage of the Upper East Side, The Surrey combines Art Deco with contemporary design to offer timeless elegance. Originally built in 1926, The Surrey has long stood as one of the great addresses of the Upper East Side, renowned for its refined character and quiet sophistication. Reopening in 2024 as Corinthia Hotels’ first property in the US, the hotel enters a new chapter, its design thoughtfully reimagined to reflect both its storied past and the spirit of modern New York. MBDS reimagines the hotel’s rooms, suites, spa, and public areas, bringing a layered and nuanced approach to the interiors. Sumptuous materials and finely crafted details honour the building’s heritage while introducing a fresh, modern expression. The Surrey’s interiors strike a careful balance between a welcoming, residential spirit and a reverence for the building’s architectural heritage. At its core is the idea of ‘sublime comfort’ , a design philosophy that creates a sense of ease and belonging for every guest. History and modernity converge to shape a distinct expression of luxury, one that reflects the Corinthia ethos while capturing the Upper East Side’s refined charm. Through a blend of rich materials and a contemporary classic layered style, the hotel has an atmosphere that feels both refined and residential. MARTIN BRUDNIZKI The hotel’s four signature suites are inspired by the bridges of nearby Central Park. Each suite features bespoke crown mouldings that echo the character of a different bridge, paired with hand-painted illustrations inside the armoire, creating a dialogue between craftsmanship and place. The Surrey Spa is a serene retreat wrapped in marble, where soft curves and a warm, neutral palette create an enveloping sense of calm. Designed to echo Corinthia’s world-renowned approach to wellness, the space invites guests to pause, restore, and emerge renewed - a quiet counterpoint to the energy of the Upper East Side. Selected works

items.title: Splendido, Portofino — MBDS
items.text: PORTOFINO Splendido Preserving its legacy as the ‘Grande Dame of Portofino’, Belmond’s Splendido is a timeless retreat on the Ligurian coast and an icon of Italian hospitality. The design situates guests in Portofino, creating a comforting feeling of being at a friend’s holiday home, while allowing them to experience the beauty, art, and life of this magical place. Martin Brudnizki Formerly a 16th-century Benedictine monastery, Splendido is steeped in history, framed by lush gardens, pastel façades and the romance of la dolce vita. MBDS approached the transformation with deep respect, reimagining the hotel as a grand coastal villa. A layered, residential approach ensures it feels intimate, characterful and unmistakably Italian. Furnishings sourced from local estate sales and auction houses tell a story of heritage, with some pieces delicately restored in the Genoese style. The suites channel the charm of a well-travelled aristocrat, complete with curated antiques and timeworn treasures. BRITISH VOGUE Splendido pays tribute to traditional techniques and local craftsmanship while also feeling resolutely contemporary. More than a hotel, Splendido is an immersive experience of Portofino’s beauty and culture. Every detail, from craft to comfort, has been designed to celebrate the charm, artistry, and enduring spirit of the Italian Riviera. Selected works

items.title: Villa Beatrice, Portofino — MBDS
items.text: PORTOFINO Villa Beatrice A storied 19th-century villa, Villa Beatrice at Belmond's Splendido has been reborn with quiet grandeur above the shimmering Ligurian coast. Built in the 19th century, Villa Beatrice was originally conceived as a summer residence for hosting grand gatherings of family and friends. Found in one of the most coveted locations on the Gulf of Portofino, the villa perches on a promontory just above Punta Caiega to offer breathtaking views over the Ligurian Riviera. In a captivating blend of Gothic Revival charm and Art Nouveau materiality and techniques, Villa Beatrice is a true architectural gem that Belmond and MBDS have solicitously brought back to life. Villa Beatrice is a place where modern sophistication meets the spirit of a cherished family home — lovingly preserved and enriched through generations on the Ligurian coast. MARTIN BRUDNIZKI Martin’s approach echoes Ligurian living at its most honest. Take, for example, the Italian fabrics from regional mills used in the linens and embroidery of curtains. The full façade, once adorned with vibrant murals, has been carefully restored from the top down to unveil intricate designs and deep terracotta tones, while the villa’s grand arches, windows, and frescoed walls and ceilings have all been uplifted using artisanal preservation techniques. WALLPAPER* Selected works

items.title: Broadwick Soho, London — MBDS
items.text: LONDON Broadwick Soho In tribute to vibrant Soho, Broadwick is inspired by gritty glamour with influences that range from 1970s disco pop to British eccentricity. Broadwick Soho is a celebration of the neighbourhood, a destination that feels as though it has always been there, evolving with cultural shifts and dynamics. Martin Brudnizki In homage to the diverse history of Soho and the strong women who frequented Soho during the 1960s and 70s, MBDS have crafted a design approach summarised as Studio 54 meets your grandmother’s townhouse . Throughout the hotel design, a mix of materials, c olours and textures have been used to encapsulate an eclectic look in a tribute to the vibrant essence of this iconic London neighbourhood. Each of Broadwick Soho's meticulously designed rooms and suites serves as a tranquil and rejuvenating retreat , featuring bespoke furniture, and thoughtfully chosen artworks by MBDS. In the suites, the walls are swathed in marbled wallpaper, a backdrop to a captivating tableau of floating elephants, tigers, and exotic flora and fauna, presented in an enchanting hand-drawn style. The mini bars masquerade as brass elephants, effortlessly blending practicality with whimsical aesthetics. Crafted in Jaipur, India by masterful artisans, each mini bar underwent meticulous design and crafting procedures to attain flawlessness. Throw in touches of Italian romanticism and disco fabulousness, all carried out through an incredible assortment of colors, textures, and bespoke fabrics and materials. The corner-to-corner details of Broadwick’s décor are truly something to behold. FORBES Selected works

items.title: Le Grand Mazarin, Paris — MBDS
items.text: PARIS Le Grand Mazarin Situated in the heart of Le Marais, Le Grand Mazarin is inspired by the way in which the area tells the story of Paris’ cultural history. We were inspired by the concept of the salon, where figures from art, literature, and music gathered in sumptuous residences, exchanging ideas and thoughts. Martin Brudnizki From its aristocratic foundations to the city’s entwined love of the arts, MBDS has designed a neighbourhood hotel that brings together history, art and literature in a thoroughly Parisian way. Inspired by the great salons of a bygone era, the studio sought to reinvent the concept of the home as being a place of entertainment for the culturally aware and progressive, where like-minded souls can gather, dine and sleep . Each space takes you on a journey through the salon host’s eyes and experiences. There is a collector’s feel to each space with layered detailing, bespoke furniture and lighting and antique items and accessories , all of which mirror the host’s well-lived life, her adventures and loves. There is a slightly different feel for each part of the host’s journey and exploration through different countries, yet there is a strong thread throughout the whole property that ties everything together in a cohesive manner. Every corner of this jewel box hotel has been thought through, from the artfully arranged alcoves and bookshelves in the lobby to the gorgeous mural painted by local artist Jacques Merle above the indoor swimming pool. EVENING STANDARD Selected works

items.title: Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's, New York — MBDS
items.text: NEW YORK Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's Hotel Barriere Fouquet’s is a 97 guestroom and suite hotel located in the historic Tribeca neighborhood in New York. We have a hotel that emanates a distinctly Parisian ambience whilst ensuring it is in keeping with its downtown site. Martin Brudnizki The first US operation for the iconic French hotelier Lucien Barriere, the hotel opened in 2022 and features Brasserie Fouquet’s New York, Par Ici Café, Titsou Bar and also a spa. The design brought together high glamour, colour and elegance in a modern and timeless way whilst leaning on the building’s architecture which blends seamlessly into the Tribeca landscape, with its unique Downtown feeling. Mixing together mohair velvets and high gloss burr walnut as well as sleek veneer in the reception and antique mirror detailing, our layered approach creates a welcoming and warm atmosphere that will make the new hotel feel as though it has always been a part of the Tribeca landscape. UPTOWN MEETS DOWNTOWN Hotel Barriere Fouquet’s is a chic reminder of small scale elegance and comfort. Selected works

items.title: Rhinecliff Residence
items.text: Rhinecliff Residence Post Company Rhinecliff Residence 2024 Rhinecliff, NY Residential Role Interior Design Scope Single Family Residence Partners Contractor: NY Renaissance Group Project Narrative This is a home of warmth, intimacy, grace and precision. While conservative on square footage, the spaces are efficient and thoughtful, a dance where utility has been conceived as an opportunity for beauty. The goal was to embrace the quirks and unique conditions of this 1860's historic home while making it a contemporary expression of the homeowners and their interests. The philosophy was to create a rhythm of light and dark, restraint and saturation. Smaller, more intimate spaces are flooded with color and texture — a red mudroom, an earthy guest room, or a bath fully built out of Calacatta Rosa marble, while more open spaces are painted in subtly shifting tones of limewash. The furniture represents a collection of contemporary works, as well as vintage sourced throughout the Hudson valley.

items.title: La Playa Hotel
items.text: La Playa Hotel Post Company La Playa Hotel 2023 Carmel, CA Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design Scope Renovation: 67 Room Hotel, F&B Outlets (Bud's), Lobby, Pool, Outdoor Spaces Partners Owner: Marc and Rose Architects: Synectic Design Contractor: Arsenio Branding: Alex Rinker Photography: Chris Mottalini Project Narrative Originally constructed in 1905 by the artist Christian Jorgensen as a gift to his wife Angela, daughter and heiress of the Ghiradelli family fortune. In 1922, the property became a hotel with rooms costing a whopping $2.50 a day. La Playa has continued to evolve alongside the community, "maintaining its eccentric charm and reputation as a haven for writers and artists." Carmel has always been a place of inclusion among California's rock and severe coastal landscape, a place that encourages irreverent thought and exploration. While historic and classic in its architecture and bones, La Playa’s charm and approach is curious and spry. The design of the hotel honors its history and vernacular while ushering in the works and objects of contemporary artists and muses. The resulting effortless eclecticism spans era and trend.

items.title: The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club
items.text: The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club Post Company The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club 2023 San Diego, CA Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design Scope Renovation: 139 Room Hotel, F&B Outlets (Quixote, The Gutter, Beginner’s Diner, Le Horse, Lulu’s, The Mississippi Room), Lobby, Cafe, Pool, Outdoor Spaces Partners Owner: Consortium Holdings Architects: Tucker Sadler Contractor: CLTVT, Hawkins Construction, ADK Studios Project Narrative The new LaFayette Hotel & Club brings guests on a creative exploration that features an ode to the original “city within a city” hotel concept moving beyond a one-dimensional space that exudes well curated affluence with aspirational style. Accessible luxury can be found in each of the hotel’s food & beverage vignettes and the 139 rooms featuring custom designed linens and a thoughtfully curated in-room bar amenity featuring a comprehensive spirit and cocktail set-up by venerable cocktail expert Paul McGee. The Lobby Bar iscircular in design under the soaring glass atrium flooding the space with light and is anchored by the Atlas statue and surrounded by a hand-painted ceiling by Brazilian-based artist Joāo Incerti. The bar is constructed with detailed wood surrounded by delicate banquettes with wrought iron lamps and is a convenient meeting space and starting point to the many dining and entertainment rooms held within the hotel. The LaFayette Hotel and Swim Club is home to a range of guest rooms, suites, and townhouses rooted in traditional Victorian, Tudor, and Gothic details. Rich saturations of color, texture, and pattern immerse guests in a fanciful experience that is much more than just a place of rest. Design elements such as wallpaper ceilings, saturated wall tones, fabric draped canopy beds, and burled bar carts read as functional sculpture or art.

items.title: Cafe Zaffri
items.text: Cafe Zaffri Post Company Cafe Zaffri 2025 New York, NY Food & Beverage Role Interior Design, Branding & Identity Scope Restaurant: Interior Design and Branding Partners Client: Elizabeth Street Hospitality & The Twenty-Two Photographer: Gentl & Hyers Project Narrative The building itself, an idea ahead of it’s time, holds a unique history. Commissioned by heiress Margaret Louisa Vanderbilt in 1891, it was was built for enterprising women, a symbol of agency and voice. Here, a new women-led institution elbows through, and like all true New York establishments, a space that reinvents heritage through irreverent iconoclasm. White tablecloths are an invitation for evidence of enjoyment, celebration, and revelry. Contradiction is at the heart of the Zaf’s concept, one that elevates the exceptional, questions the traditions of hospitality, and provides opportunity for unconventional gatherings and surprising guests. Within the formal and historied architecture of The Twenty-Two, inside a room dripping with luxury lies a story of expression, rebellion, and exuberance. Across interiors and branding , we developed a narrative that balances formality and play. Custom silk wallpaper and tasseled menu books are invitations for long dinners with multiple martinis and fries for the table.

items.title: INNESS
items.text: INNESS Post Company INNESS 2021 Accord, NY Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Building Design, Interior Design, Development Scope New Construction: 40 Room Hotel, Pools, Grounds, Restaurant & Bar, Greenhouse Shop, Outfitter, Gatehouse, Event Barn, Spa & Gym, Golf Course, Tennis Courts Partners Designed in Collaboration: Taavo Somer Development Partners: Taavo Somer, CBSK Ironstate, Lee Pollock Architect: Dutton Architecture Landscape: Miranda Brooks Landscape Design Contractor: RL Baxter Collaborators: Adsum, Beall and Bell, Blended LA, Episode, Holler and Squall, King Collins Golf, Libeco Home, Morentz Gallery, Devon Ojas, Pidjin, Plain English Kitchens, Roll and Hill, Sixpenny, Sonos, WaterWorks, Michael Williams, Works Mfg Photographer: Adrian Gaut Styling: Colin King Project Narrative INNESS is an intimate country refuge and members club located in Accord, New York – about 90 minutes outside New York City. Situated on 225 pastoral acres, its sprawling campus includes 40 hotel rooms (28 cabins, and a 12 room farmhouse), a restaurant and lounge, a 9-hole golf course designed by King Collins, a sports outfitter, swimming pools, tennis courts, hiking trails, an events barn, a farm shop, as well as a 3-acre organic farm embedded into grounds imagined by landscape designer Miranda Brooks. Named after the prominent American landscape painter George Inness, INNESS was conceived by a collaborative team who regularly escaped the city to immerse themselves in the natural spoils of the Hudson Valley. INNESS is a respite from urban living, rooted in the comfort and contentment of the shared experience. A cultural epicenter framed by a stunning landscape.

items.title: Longfellow Hotel
items.text: Longfellow Hotel Post Company Longfellow Hotel 2024 Portland, ME Hotel, Food & Beverage Role Interior Design, Branding & Identity Scope New Construction: Guest rooms, Lobby, Bar, Cafe, Meeting Spaces, & Spa Partners Owner: Uncommon Hospitality Architect: Archetype Photography: Carly Rudd, Chris Mottalini Project Narrative The Longfellow is named for Portland native Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, whose poems drew inspiration from the wild, untamed beauty of the New England coast. Much like the famed poet’s enduring words, the hotel reflects the location’s rugged charm and extremes of the environment - from cold, blustery winters to sun-soaked summer months. "Often I think of thetown that is seated by the sea." — From "My Lost Youth," Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
