items.title: The Brand — Tatjana von Stein
items.text: MANIFESTO From art to spirituality, psychology to design, no realm is closed to exploration. In design, there is freedom in fluidity . BRAND & Culture Tatjana von Stein is an interior architecture, interior design, and furniture design studio with a global reach. The studio is headquartered in London, serving international projects high-end residential, luxury hotels, members’ clubs, and creative spaces across the across the world. In response to growing demand and a deep appreciation for local craftsmanship, the studio expanded to Mallorca in 2025, establishing a base to service the Balearic Islands and the Mediterranean region. This presence allows for more intimate collaborations with local artisans, bringing a focus on materiality and craftsmanship, and creating spaces deeply rooted in the Mediterranean context. The studio is known for creating intuitive, immersive interiors that reflect the unique character of each project. Founder & Creative Director Tatjana von Stein combines her French/German heritage with a thoughtful approach to the psychology of space, blending historical references with contemporary design. Her versatile approach ensures that each space is timeless yet relevant, with a subtle connection between past and present. This commitment to meaningful, enduring spaces shapes both the studio’s interiors and design collectibles. In 2023, the studio launched Mise en Scène , its first collection of design collectibles, produced in collaboration with some of France’s finest artisans. The collection embodies the same dedication to craftsmanship, materiality, and timeless design that defines their interiors. THE FOUNDER Tatjana von Stein CONTACT TATJANA POSITIVE IMPACT A continuing journey 01. ARTISANS We strive to be thoughtful when sourcing our materials, opting for the most responsible options wherever possible. Considerations include supply chain and renewability — things that help us minimise our impact on the natural world. As part of our journey to make a positive impact, we are continually exploring all our options. 02. MATERIALS In our ongoing commitment to positive change within the design industry, we have a dedicated partnership with the Royal Society of Arts. Through the RSA network we are able to contribute to the development of emerging designers working to find solutions to the social and environmental issues we face today. 03. SUPPORTING THE ARTS Impact is a journey, and transparency is key. We know there are areas where we can do better, and we'll always strive to do so. In the meantime, we will continue to be open and honest about the impact we're having, paying close attention to our carbon footprint and exploring all the options to help us improve. 04. HONESTY Collaboration has been key in helping us sustain our values of quality, transparency, and craft excellence. We have partnered with Aurige, the French heritage conservation group who, with over 75 years' experience, have brought together a collective of specialist artisans dedicated to upholding design integrity and creating products that are made to last. IMPACT STATEMENT

items.title: Positive Impact — Tatjana von Stein
items.text: POSITIVE IMPACT Our ongoing journey. DISCOVER THE COLLECTION RESPONSIBLY MADE Here, at Tatjana von Stein, we are committed to a greener future. Behind every creation is a team dedicated to minimising our footprint while maintaining superior quality. As research continues and technology advances, we are dedicated to change, adaptation, and evolution across each area of the business to ensure we can streamline processes, minimise waste and increase efficiency. Our purpose is to ensure the designs we create not only stand the test of time but prioritise responsible design principles from the outset. In partnering with independent artisanal workshops to cut across the mass manufacturing cycles which plague the industry today, we have full control over the production methods used and the materials sourced. In understanding the responsibility we have as designers, and with a mission to create heirlooms of the future, we know we can contribute towards a more accountable creative sector. Our journey is just beginning and, while we are very aware that there is room for improvement in reducing our carbon footprint, we are committed to sharing our experience with you to ensure full transparency is maintained. As it is often quoted, sustainability is a journey, not a destination, and through effective changes one step at a time, we will continue to fight for a future which protects and serves both people and planet simultaneously. We are also dedicated to creating a more diverse industry and will be investing back into the creative sectors to ensure we can support equal opportunities for all. With an honest approach and our unwavering commitment to a sustainable design industry, we will be refining our processes year on year. Design can be a powerful force for change and here, at Tatjana von Stein, we hope to exemplify that. ARTISANAL EXPERTISE Collaborating with external partners has been key in sustaining our values of quality, transparency, and craft excellence. We have partnered with Aurige, the French heritage conservation group who, with 78 years of experience, have brought together a collective of specialist artisans who uphold design integrity through a strong understanding of creating products that are made to last. Being the only company in France which offers a complete selection of trades dedicated to heritage restoration, we are proud to work alongside Aurige and the extensive knowledge and grasp of craft they have. Not only does this provide access to some of the best artisans across the country, but it also gives us confidence knowing that we are helping to preserve valuable skillsets and techniques which have been used for centuries. Aurige is committed to offering pathways for young apprentices to learn such crafts helping to pass these dexterities down and sustaining them for generations to come. QUALITY MATERIALS Using the finest materials possible, we manufacture each item to order to ensure maximum efficiency of all resources used. Working closely with our makers and artisans, we opt for materials which are located as closely to the workshops as possible. Through sourcing locally where possible, we can minimise our logistical footprint as well as ensuring we obtain the highest quality ingredients possible. With each design, we publicly list every material used to provide full transparency to our clients. With our furniture manufacturing studio based in France and our textile workshops based in Portugal, we are committed to working with local creative communities who fully understand and respect the materials they are working with. items.title: Acerca de mi | Ruben Cabrera
items.text: ¡Hola! soy Rubén "De las Ventas Farmacéuticas al Marketing y Comercio en Canales Digitales" Una historia de evolucion marcada por la pandemia COVID-19 y los adelantos tecnologicos acelerados que desde entonces han surgido. Quiero ayudarte a crear estrategias de marketing y comercio digital dentro de las limitaciones que supone el sector salud en Colombia y el resto del mundo. Donde todo comenzó: Aprender a vender es entender a las personas. Hace más de una década, mi camino profesional comenzó en el mundo farmacéutico. Durante más de 13 años, fui responsable de gestionar cuentas clave, diseñar estrategias de ventas y establecer relaciones comerciales con cadenas nacionales y regionales de droguerías y profesionales de la salud. En este sector, aprendí que vender un producto no es solo una transacción, sino un proceso que requiere confianza, conocimiento profundo del mercado y estrategias bien estructuradas. El mundo cambia y yo con él: La transformación digital llegó para quedarse. Con el tiempo, comprendí que la forma en que las empresas y los consumidores interactúan evolucionaba con rapidez. El marketing digital comenzó a transformar la manera en que las marcas llegaban a su público. Vi la oportunidad y decidí no quedarme atrás: me sumergí en el estudio del marketing digital y el aprovechamiento de las tecnologias web, descubriendo un nuevo mundo lleno de posibilidades. De la estrategia comercial a la digital: Conectar mundos para multiplicar resultados. Lo que comenzó como una necesidad de adaptación se convirtió en mi nueva pasión. Aprendí a crear estrategias digitales efectivas, diseñar sitios web optimizados para la conversión y lanzar campañas publicitarias que generan resultados. Me di cuenta de que mis habilidades en ventas, análisis de mercado y negociación eran perfectamente aplicables en este nuevo entorno, permitiéndome conectar ambos mundos: la venta tradicional y la transformación digital. Hoy, ayudo a las empresas a: Crecer en un mundo digitalizad. Actualmente, combino mi experiencia en el sector farmacéutico con mis conocimientos en marketing y publicidad digital para ayudar a empresas del sector salud, belleza y otros sectores a expandir su presencia online, optimizar sus estrategias comerciales y desarrollar nuevos canales de distribución y ventas. Sé cómo abordar los desafíos del mercado, conectar con los clientes adecuados y diseñar estrategias que realmente funcionan. La clave del éxito: Adaptarse, innovar y encontrar oportunidades. Si algo he aprendido en este viaje es que la clave del éxito radica en la capacidad de adaptarse, innovar y ver oportunidades donde otros solo ven obstáculos. Estoy aquí para ayudarte a llevar tu negocio al siguiente nivel. Algunas Marcas PARA LAS QUE HE TRABAJADO. Mas de 10 años aprendiendo continuamente Licenciatura en Administracion de Empresas Una cosa tuve claro en el año 2009, despues de sumergirme en el mundo de las negocioaciones B2B entre las empresas, decidi tomar como profesion el arte de entender profundamente la forma en que necesitan funcionar las empresas como un todo. Diplomado en Oratoria Una vez en el mundo de las ventas y la gestion empresarial, en el 2011 me di cuenta que para ser un buen vendedor, negociador y gestor es indispensable aprender hablar en publico y comunicar de la mejor manera posible ideas claras y motivadoras. Certificacion Marketing Digital Despues de acumular 8 años de experiencia gestionando Cuentas Clave, afrontando negocioaciones relevantes y gestionando equipos de venta; en el 2020 producto de la PANDEMIA COVID-19 me di cuenta que las herramientas de marketing y ventas digitales son capaces de traer a cualquier negocio nuevas y mejores oportunidades para su crecimiento, desde entonces decidi capacitarme para afrontar los nuevos retos de comunicacion y ventas para las empresas del sector salud y otros. items.title: À propos • Rodolphe Parente • Rodolphe Parente
items.text: EN Presse Rodolphe Parente fonde son studio à Paris en 2009 après avoir exercé plusieurs années aux côtés d’Andrée Putman. Cette expérience lui permet de manier l’architecture intérieure comme le design ; une vision globale de l’espace qu’il apprend à maîtriser lors de ses études à l’Ecole Nationale des Beaux-Arts de Dijon, puis à l’Ecole supérieure des arts décoratifs de Strasbourg et à l’ECAL, l'Ecole d'art et de design de Lausanne. Rodolphe Parente conserve au sein de son studio cette volonté d’hétérogénéité et les atouts de sa double formation. Il conçoit des projets aux échelles de création et destinations variées : résidentiel, hôtels , restaurants , salles de sport, châteaux, bureaux, banques, boutiques, mobilier et accessoires. Les affinités et influences esthétiques de Rodolphe Parente comptent notamment l’esprit novateur des années 30, le glamour des années 70 ou la radicalité des années 80. Ces courants forts ont forgé son goût et son esprit libre. L’ingéniosité, la sensibilité à l’artisanat, l’expressivité des matières, une certaine fantaisie et l’ouverture aux usages contemporains sont ainsi distillés et sublimés dans ses projets. Tous témoignent de ce désir d’imaginaire, de contraste et de justesse, de modernité sans cesse réinventée. Ses réalisations préconisent un luxe teinté de légèreté, prônent la curiosité et honore l’art. Le confort et l’harmonie d’un lieu passent par la luminosité, la mise en valeur de textures singulières, des jeux de volumes étudiés, des couleurs architecturées qui révèleront une pièce. Rodolphe Parente affectionne également les croisements et les détails inattendus, les hommages à la fois décalés et suggérés. Les codes sont ainsi subtilement déjoués, garantissant des lieux non stéréotypés. Chaque nouveau projet implique la recherche du ton juste et des choix légitimes. Ce désir de narration est toujours le fruit d’une réflexion sensible au profit du destinataire. Il ne s’agit pas d’appliquer une recette ni d’être la démonstration mais de créer des lieux sur mesure, adéquats. Les réalisations signées Rodolphe Parente ne se ressemblent pas, il s’attèle à proposer à chaque fois une nouvelle écriture. Le parti pris peut être tour à tour radical, sophistiqué, hybride, enveloppant. Pour chacun de ses projets, la volonté de Rodolphe Parente est d’accompagner, d’initier, de s’inscrire dans un contexte, de susciter la curiosité afin de réaliser des lieux naturellement incarnés et vivants. A l’été 2022, Rodolphe Parente fut Président du Jury et invité d’honneur de la Design Parade Toulon, 6 ème festival international d'architecture d'intérieur. Il a présenté à cette occasion l’exposition « Contre-soirée » dans l’Ancien Évêché. Pour honorer cette carte blanche, Rodolphe Parente a délivré un message festif, une ode à la générosité et au partage, à travers des jeux de lumière, de textures, de rythmes et d’assemblages qu’il aime tant maîtriser. Cette proposition personnelle et scénographique, volontairement intergénérationnelle, affirme ainsi son écriture et marque son parcours. items.title: HALF EMPTY — BRE FURLONG
items.text: HALF EMPTY — BRE FURLONG Menu When I was first handed my daughter, all I could think of was the cicadas on my front steps when I was a kid, dried up and shaking in the wind. A shell left behind, so that someone else could thrive. I was empty, but when I first held her, I fed her. And for a while, that’s all I could do. Just a cicada and a tree. Two years later, I’m still breastfeeding my child. Outside of childbirth, it has been the most challenging thing I've ever done. Instead of putting language to it, I decided to explore it visually. This is a recollection of my breastfeeding journey, Half Empty. Published HERE , by It’s Nice That.

The Elevine Silver Stone Brooch | Pendant is a smooth shape inspired by the many river rocks gleaned from walks and journeys, or given from friends, that have found their way into Elevine's pockets and onto her desk. This hand carved piece cast in solid sterling silver reveals a ring to fit a chain as well as a handmade pin mechanism, allowing it to be worn both as a brooch and a pendant. Offered made to order by the Brooklyn jewelry studio Dunton Ellerkamp , in two sizes with two accompanying chain options. items.title: Traces of Impermanence – MW Editions
items.text: Books Traces of Impermanence By Lauren Shaw Essays by Lucy R. Lippard and Terry Tempest Williams $ 55.00 Hardbound 10 x 10 inches 96 pages 61 color photographs ISBN: 9781969303074 Description Additional information As a young girl growing up in the American South, photographer Lauren Shaw watched her mother with fascination as she prepared for a night out. After lightly misting her hairspray to set her coif, she reached for a small jar of silver glitter resting on the counter and, with the delicate touch of her index finger, carefully dabbed it onto several strands along her hairline. She gazed approvingly into the mirror—she was dazzling, and she knew it. Shaw’s mother maintained her well-groomed appearance at all times, even as she kept a watchful eye on her children as they played along the sun-drenched shores of Daytona Beach. Her closet was meticulously ordered, each dress in its own plastic bag, shoe boxes carefully stacked: This was her arsenal in the battle against the passage of time. Later in life, Shaw’s mother was struck by Alzheimer’s disease, and her impeccable self-presentation began to crumble. As Shaw began to examine her own relationship to aging, she realized her mother’s armor of attractiveness—her vanity—maintained her sense of self in a world that inevitably pushed her toward aging. Traces of Impermanence explores the transient power in both nature and the human body through photographs that examine the cycles of growth, decay, and renewal, reflecting the rhythms that govern all living things. In this series, Shaw documents her body yielding to the natural progression of time—its scars, bruises, and marks reflecting resilience, vulnerability, and a record of a life lived. These are juxtaposed with poetic images from the natural world, showing the interplay between beauty and imperfection, growth and decay, each shaping and deepening the presence of the other. Along with Shaw’s own written reflections on aging, Traces of Impermanence contains essays by esteemed art critic Lucy Lippard and writer and activist Terry Tempest Williams. Additional information Weight 1.75 lbs Dimensions 10 × 10 × .75 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Lauren Shaw received her MFA in photography from the Rhode Island School of Design, where she studied with Harry Callahan and Aaron Siskind. She is Professor Emerita of Photography at Emerson College in Boston and a co-founder of New England Women in Photography. Shaw's work has been exhibited widely throughout the United States and is in the permanent collections of the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; Fogg Museum, Harvard University, Cambridge; High Museum of Art, Atlanta; Art Institute of Chicago; The Newark Museum of Art, NJ; Farnsworth Art Museum, Rockland, ME; and the Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. Her multimedia project Maine Women: Living on the Land (2005)—which included a photographic installation, a book, and a documentary film—was exhibited at the Farnsworth Art Museum and traveled throughout the United States. Her documentary films include: A Drop in the Bucket (2010), Angkor's Children (2014), If They Had Known (2016), About John (2019), and Routine Interrupted (2022). Shaw lives and works in Boston.

items.title: Injection Site – MW Editions
items.text: Books Injection Site By Linda Alterwitz Essay by Leah Ollman $ 55.00 Clothbound with jacket 9 x 10 inches 112 pages 65 black and white photographs ISBN: 9781969303036 Description Additional information In early 2021, more than a year after the Covid-19 pandemic began, vaccines for the disease had finally become available. Photographer Linda Alterwitz was curious about the vaccine’s effects after a neighbor complained of continued pain in her arm nine days after she received it. Using a camera that registers heat, rather than light, Alterwitz was astonished to see dark, contrasting patterns on her friend’s arm that spread out toward her breast and shoulder. This photograph—intimate, ephemeral, scientific, and moving—led to Injection Site , in which she photographed the arms of more than 130 participants from 2021to 2023. Alterwitz explained to each person that she was using a heat camera to make thermographic images, rendering visible their bodies’ reactions to the Covid vaccine. She emphasized to the participants that it was not a scientific experiment, but a unique way of documenting the pandemic. Injection Site illustrates a moment when the entire world faced a common threat and extends the ongoing examination of how Covid-19 has shaped our collective consciousness. The photographs—showing spidery networks of veins, splotches, and other visible marks of inflammation in the human body—provoke curiosity about how our experiences could be simultaneously intensely individual but also universal. Although the memory of the pandemic may no longer sit at the forefront of our minds, it continues to create anxiety about our future. We continue to live amid a perfect storm of global warming, overpopulation, habitat loss, and global migration that brings us ever closer to the next planetary threat. Additional information Weight 2 lbs Dimensions 9 × 10 × 1 in About the Author Linda Alterwitz is an interdisciplinary artist with a focus on photography. Her practice centers on the unseen rhythms of the human body and our relationship to the natural world, encouraging dialogue on choice, trust, and collective experience. Alterwitz endured a health crisis in the late 1990s, which transformed her practice as she began to combine art and science in her image creation. In 2024, the New York Times selected an Injection Site portrait to accompany an essay by the immunologist Dr. Rick Bright, who filed a whistleblower complaint against the first Trump administration for ignoring his warnings about national preparedness for the Covid-19 pandemic. Alterwitz exhibited Injection Site at FORMAT International Photography Festival, Derby, UK, in 2025 and at Ulrich Museum of Art at Wichita State University, Kansas, in conjunction with the WSU School of Nursing in 2026. Her work is held in permanent collections including The Institute for Art + Environment at Nevada Museum of Art in Reno; Center for Creative Photography, Tucson; Getty Research Institute, Los Angeles; Hilliard Art Museum, Lafayette, LA; Spencer Art Reference Library, Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City, MO; Constance and George Fearing Library, Santa Barbara Museum of Art, Santa Barbara, CA; Wallace Library, Rochester Institute of Technology; Marjorie Barrick Museum, University of Nevada, Las Vegas; and the Lilley Museum of Art, University of Nevada, Reno. Alterwitz lives and works in Las Vegas.

items.title: Leviathan Rising – MW Editions
items.text: Books Leviathan Rising By Eirik Johnson Essays by Sam Hockley-Smith and Sylvia Wolf $ 75.00 Hardcover 10 x 13.375 inches 92 pages 68 color 3 gatefolds ISBN: 9781969303067 Description Additional information Alone in a small sea kayak, photographer Eirik Johnson floats along Washington State’s Duwamish River beneath the massive hulls of transoceanic barges, making photographs from these surreal spaces. The vessels that travel along the Inside Passage carrying goods to and from Alaskan waters to ports along the Pacific Rim often port in the Duwamish, a deeply polluted river ecosystem that flows into the Salish Sea. The photographs in Leviathan Rising capture the patinated exteriors of these beastly structures and transform scale, perspective, and light. Angular steel ribs jut out from the sterns and bows overhead, while sunlight radiates geometric patterns across their oil-slicked and rusted skins. Towering fins slice up from the water’s edge. Hidden portals uncover layers of salt and sunbaked runoff, vestiges of repeated oceanic journeys. Each layer of sediment, diesel, tar, and marine life that collects on the hulls is a marker of their voyages and of the broader system of oceanic trade. Leviathan Rising also contains a series of unique daguerreotype photograms, created in collaboration with Daniel Carrillo, depicting glass floats used by early-twentieth-century Japanese fishermen to suspend their nets in the Pacific Ocean. If the floats broke free from their netting, the ocean’s currents conveyed the spheres east, ultimately reaching the shores of the Pacific Northwest. The reflective surface of these silver plates contains the frozen imprint of each float’s journey across the Pacific. Sylvia Wolf, director emerita of the Henry Art Gallery, University of Washington, contributes an essay on a site-specific installation of this body of work, and LA-based musician and writer Sam Hockley-Smith addresses the sound component of the exhibited work, composed of aquatic field recordings that Johnson made beneath the surface of the Duwamish. Leviathan Rising ’s arresting images of the daunting structures that carry commercial cargo across global waters and these thought-provoking texts compellingly address oceanic commerce and environmental fragility in our uncertain era. Additional information Weight 2.375 lbs Dimensions 13 × 10 × .75 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Eirik Johnson makes conceptually grounded work examining the global intersections of contemporary environmental, social, and economic issues. Employing various modes of presentation from photobooks to experiential photo- and sound-based installation, Johnson's photographic and interdisciplinary projects explore the marks and connections formed in the friction of these complicated relationships. He has exhibited his work at institutions including the Aperture Foundation, New York; Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston; and the Henry Art Gallery, Seattle. Johnson's work is in the permanent collections of institutions including the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; International Center of Photography, New York; Nevada Museum of Art, Reno; and the George Eastman Museum, Rochester, NY. His previous monographs include Road to Nowhere (2021), Barrow Cabins (2019), Pine (2018), Sawdust Mountain (2009), and Borderlands (2005). Related Title Leviathan Rising (Limited Edition)

items.title: Night Journey – MW Editions
items.text: Books Night Journey By Susan kae Grant $ 70.00 Clothbound with jacket 9.25 x 12 inches 164 pages 89 black and white photographs 6 gatefolds, one section printed on translucent paper ISBN: 9781969303050 Description Additional information One morning when she was a young girl, Susan kae Grant woke from her night’s sleep and told her mother, “I went somewhere last night.” Since childhood, Grant has understood that the dream state transports her far from the material world of her bedroom. For the last twenty-five years, she has created a cycle of photographs composed of dream imagery conjured from her unconscious and from deep research into the science and magic of human sleep. In the early 1990s, Grant began collaborating with noted sleep researcher Dr. John Herman at the UT Southwestern Medical Center Sleep Laboratory, where she interrogated her own hyperactive REM sleep through controlled awakenings designed to elicit visual and verbal descriptions of the dream space. The phrases that were coaxed from her unconscious mind seeded Night Journey with a vocabulary that continues to inform her work: “Turning pages searching for a number… Not anchored by a bed… Filled with fluid… Frosted glass encounter… Sex is interrupted… These hands listening…” Night Journey delivers a haunting shadow world made up of silhouetted figures and symbolic forms that envelopes viewers in the elusive terrain of the dream state. Through arresting black and white tableaux populated by fantastical creatures, animals, and children in hallucinatory settings, these photographs invite us to traverse the strangeness and chaos of breakneck contemporary life, like the dreams that inspired them. In nearly a hundred photographs, along with essays by Deboarh Willis with Mecca Brooks and Trudy Wilner Stack, Night Journey engages dream and memory as a portal into the mysterious space of sleep we all share. Additional information Weight 3 lbs Dimensions 12 × 9.25 × 1.5 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Susan kae Grant is an inventive and influential lens-based artist and educator. She has participated in exhibitions across the United States, Canada, China, Europe, Australia, British Columbia, Africa, Guatemala, and Japan. Her work is in the permanent collections of George Eastman Museum, Rochester, New York; J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; Minneapolis Institute of Art; Tokyo Photographic Museum; Victoria & Albert National Art Library, London; Center for Creative Photography, Tucson; and Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Grant holds both an MFA and a BS in photography and book arts from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She teaches workshops at prestigious institutions such as The International Center of Photography, New York; Los Angeles Center for Photography; La Luz Workshops; Maine Media Workshops, and Santa Fe Workshops. She is represented by Conduit Gallery in Dallas.

items.title: Deer – MW Editions
items.text: Books Deer By Tanya Marcuse $ 55.00 Clothbound with tipped-on image 10 x 12 inches 36 pages 16 color photographs ISBN: 979-8-9879085-2-5 Co-published with ROMAN NVMERALS Description Additional information On September 8, 2023, photographer Tanya Marcuse photographed a deer that died near the woods. She returned repeatedly to photograph the deer until its body disappeared nineteen months later, in April 2025. What unfolds in these photographs is not a straightforward chronicle of decomposition, but a metaphysical transformation, as the deer seems to unravel into the universe. Through embellishments that verge on the alchemical, including the use of fire, Marcuse’s photographs transform the deer’s body into a portal from the terrestrial to the celestial, from matter to myth. Tanya Marcuse’s work investigates cycles of life and decay, and photography’s capacity to probe what lies beyond empirical fact. Deer extends this inquiry to its most distilled form. At once lavish and unflinching, these sixteen images hover between fantasy and fact, evoking an enigmatic hybrid of Ana Mendieta’s ritualistic earthworks and the dense symbolism of medieval tapestries. David Campany writes in his essay, “Any place photographed becomes a stage, if only because it is in the nature of a camera to dramatize, turning what is photographed, and even the very place itself, into signs. Enigmatic signs, but signs nonetheless. To photograph a corpse in its resting place, then, is to stage its stage, and to image its image.” Deer features a special insert composed of fragments of Marcuse’s own writings, written in the second person and addressed directly to the deer. Additional information Weight 1.375 lbs Dimensions 10 × 12 × .5 in About the Author Tanya Marcuse (born 1964) is an American photographer known for her large-scale photographs that explore the imperiled natural world. She employs fantastical imagery and elaborate methods of construction to explore cycles of growth and decay and the dynamic tension between the passage of time and the photographic medium. Marcuse began making photographs as student at Bard College at Simon’s Rock before studying art history and studio art at Oberlin College. She earned her MFA from Yale University. Her work is held in public collections, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Denver Art Museum, the George Eastman Museum in Rochester, the National Gallery of Art in Washington D.C., the Baltimore Museum of Art, and the Yale University Art Gallery in New Haven. Marcuse is the recipient of numerous honors, including a Guggenheim Foundation Fellowship, a Peter S. Reed Grant, an American Scandinavian Fellowship, two MacDowell Fellowships and is currently a 2025–26 New York Foundation for the Arts Fellow. Her published books include Undergarments and Armor (2005), Wax Bodies (2012), Fruitless | Fallen | Woven (2019), Ink (2021), and Portent (2024). She is a dedicated student of martial arts and boxing as methods of cultivating mental and physical concentration and discipline. Marcuse teaches photography at Bard College in the Hudson Valley, New York, where she lives.

items.title: JANG – MW Editions
items.text: Books JANG By Michael Jang $ 50.00 – $ 60.00 Price range: $50.00 through $60.00 Hardbound 7 x 9.5 inches 176 pages 150 color illustrations­ ISBN: 978-1-969303-01-2 Description Additional information This volume showcases the San Francisco–based photographer Michael Jang’s stylized and self-aware street art from recent years. Early in 2021, when the city was still in the grip of the Covid-19 pandemic and ugly instances of anti-Asian sentiment were on the rise, Jang clandestinely wheat-pasted some of the images from his black-and-white photographic series The Jangs (1973) over a boarded-up Goodwill storefront on Clement Street, in the heart of San Francisco’s unofficial Chinatown. He branded his photographs with a JANG stencil logo—introducing the persona “Chef Jang,” a chain-smoking wok master—and interspersed them with hand-designed posters and graphics that parody Asian product packaging and menus. Inserted into the visual landscape of this once bustling neighborhood, Jang’s gesture was one of solidarity, belonging and ownership. In JANG , the artist captures his own ephemeral and ever-changing urban interventions in more than 100 new photographs. Additional information Weight 1.5 lbs Dimensions 9.5 × 7 × 1 in Edition Selection Standard, Signed About the Author Michael Jang spent more than four decades working as a successful commercial portrait photographer but was simultaneously creating an archive of thousands of remarkable images across several now-iconic series: The Jangs (1973), Beverly Hilton (1973), San Francisco (1973–87), Summer Weather (1983), College (1972–73), Punks & Poets (1978–80), and Garage Band (2001). Jang revealed nothing from his archive until 2001, when he submitted a selection of images for consideration to the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. His work attracted immediate acclaim. His first monograph, Who Is Michael Jang? , was published in 2019, the same year his first major retrospective exhibition was mounted at the McEvoy Foundation for the Arts. The documentary Who is Michael Jang? (dir. Michael Jacobs, 2024) debuted in May 2024 at the San Francisco Documentary Film Festival. Jang’s work is in the collections of the National Gallery of Art, the Museum of Modern Art, and SFMoMA, among others.

The planters are heavy, cubic, and almost archaic in form - but they span between their bases so that they appear to float. They are minimal and monolithic, a deliberate counterpoint to the lightness and organic abundance of the plants that they hold, combining material and formal restraint with chromatic opulence. Brut is available in three planter sizes and two base sizes. Available trough studio coucou. Year: 2026 Awards & publications: Currents. As a flexible sofa system, it can be rearranged within the space to adapt to different situations and needs. items.title: Film & Television — Lauren Arzbaecher
items.text: Writing Film & Television Our Editors Have Lots of Opinions on the Decor of Heated Rivalry Like pretty much everyone else on the internet, the AD team spent our winter break marathoning (and deeply loving!) Heated Rivalry. While we have virtually no notes on the pitch-perfect romance between rival hockey players Illya Rozanov and Shane Hollander, as design obsessives we were drawn to more than just the steamy sex scenes and glutes discourse. Read more Movie musical madness On-screen musicals have a colorful presence in cinematic history, yet have lately taken up the role of pariah. Three recent releases—The Color Purple, Wonka, and Mean Girls—were widely marketed without highlighting their musical elements. This means for the ill-informed audience member, one might sit down in the theater under no impression that they are about to see a musical. Read more I went behind-the-scenes on an 'Outlander' tour in Scotland. Here's how scenes from TV matched up to real life. Earlier this year, my sister gushed about a show that I just had to watch: Outlander . As a fan of historical fiction, I quickly became enamored with the show. When a family trip to the UK came around, we couldn't resist adding a stop in Scotland to visit some filming locations. Read more The age of the edit: beyond fancams and character compilations At its most simple level, an edit can be a compilation of one character’s best/most notable moments. Maybe it’s set to a sultry song with slow zooms on the actor’s face (it oh so often falls into this category). On the more comedic side, it may be strung together with meme photos, viral audios, and commentary by way of comic sans subtitling. Read more 'Grand Crew' is a hilarious sitcom with heart — here's why you should give this overlooked comedy a chance Grand Crew is created by Phil Augusta Jackson, a writer and producer best known for his work on Brooklyn Nine-Nine and Insecure . The sitcom follows a group of young professionals in LA as they traverse dating, new jobs, and the ups and downs of friendship. Read more For the love of watch parties With social media, the concept of a watch party has transformed. You can share the viewing experience with thousands of people online through social feeds, online chat groups, or even livestreams. Although you might not be in the room with the people you’re watching alongside, the countless perspectives, memes, and wild takes bring a sense of community—albeit somewhat chaotic—all the same. Read more Reboot, Redo, Retitle: Hollywood's Trip to the Recycling Plant TV reboots for “Twilight” and “Harry Potter” have both been announced as in the works, and honestly, I’m just tired. Is the content well really so dry that we need to reinvent movies that are barely over 10 years old? Moving at Renesmee aging speeds here!! Read more What Happened To Duane Chapman After 'Dog The Bounty Hunter' The notorious crime fighter has had a contentious public perception since he first appeared on the screen. Duane has been in and out of reality television since the A+E series concluded, though he still maintains his brazen lifestyle when the cameras aren't rolling. Read more What We Can Gain From Seeing History On Film We often look to the our past to see what was in style, what everyday experiences were like, what people cared about in any particular era. We look back to see how we have changed. Or how we haven’t. Yet in the digital age, we are all too willing to let the next trending topic on Twitter or limited tv series do the leg work for us. Read more Did 'WandaVision' Save the On-Screen Superhero? The MCU had become predictable. So predictable, that I was guessing lines before characters said them while in the theater. While Infinity War and Endgame broke the cycle of repetition to a certain extent, I was fairly ready to close the chapter on my viewing of on-screen superhero content. WandaVision pleasantly shattered that perception. Read more Damian Powers & Giannina Gibelli’s 'Love Is Blin

items.title: Music Writing — Lauren Arzbaecher
items.text: Concert Coverage Counterfeit Madison at the Englert Theatre Nina Simone is a legendary figure not only for her music, but for her ceaseless fight for social change in America. The fearless spirit of Simone was channeled into and molded by Counterfeit Madison in her Saturday night performance. Read more A Parade of Locals: A Night with Elizabeth Moen, Penny Peach Jr, and Dana T. Crowds are occupying the Englert on Saturday night, a night where a parade of local artists will take the stage. There will be songs dedicated to the person who was almost hit by Elly’s car earlier in the day, about wanting to die – but in a good way – and mouthguards. Read more Hinterland’s Last Day Filled with Sweet Music After two hot yet blissful days of music, St. Charles finally reached the last day of the Hinterland music fest. This year was the first in the festival’s history that the programming extended across three days rather than two. Read more SASAMI Shakes The Mill to its Core with Dream-Pop Guitar reverberated around room, echoing amid a complex synthesized soundscape. SASAMI had a commanding presence from the get-go, asking all audience members to come rock out with her. Read more Mission Creek Festival: Jay Som at the Englert Theatre “Hey everyone. I’m a big fan of the sitting down, relaxing,” Melina Duerte, better known by her stage name Jay Som, said as she greeted the seated crowd at the Englert Theatre on Friday night. She continued with a small grin, “We’re relaxing too.” Read more Younger Brings Femme Freshness to Witching Hour Adorned in varying combinations of black, the three members of the Iowa City-based alt-rock band took the stage familiarly, no doubt feeling at home. Smiling out at the crowd, the aura inside Gabe’s became warmer, a clear friendship between the band and audience. Read more The Warmth of Jamila Woods The yellow marquee of The Englert Theater provided a nice reprise from the spring snow floating down onto the Iowa City street. As cold and blustery as it was outside, the serene music of Jamila Woods made the Englert a warm space to spend the night. Read more The Artisanals at Gabe’s The usually dark second floor of Gabe’s was aglow from the light of a sizable yellow neon sign bearing the band’s name in a psychedelic font. The members of The Artisanals looked as if they stepped straight out of the 1970s as they took the stage, a crystal lamp and paisley rug rounding out the vintage setup of the Charleston-based five man group. Read more Columns & Features Rewriting the Rockstar Narrative For Pleaser Magazine Issue 4 Being several decades removed from the 1970s and 1980s, most representations of musicians from these bygone eras in movies, television, and books are done in a state of glamorized nostalgia. From Almost Famous to Daisy Jones and The Six, the allure of these fictionalized takes is clear. The framing of these stories, though, can dramatically impact the public perception of the musicians they’re based on, and things are never quite as simple as “it was just what they did back then.” Read more Hemlocke Springs Searches For Love in New Single “enknee1” You have likely already heard snippets of hemlocke springs’ hypnotic sound when scrolling through social media without even knowing it. Rabid use of her single “ girlfriend ” on TikTok—the audio has been used in 68.9K videos to date—brought the artist a slew of new fans since its release in November of 2022. Her latest single, “enknee1,” shows a new layer of the artist equally deserving of virality. Read more Spotify Wrapped – UNwrapped Reaching the end of the year, we look back at the music that shaped us during the last twelve months. The most popular retrospective for music listeners, Spotify Wrapped, is a gift that comes early. I looked closely into how accurately Wrapped reflects listening habits with the data it collects. Then with the help of Pleaser staff, I dove into the larger question of how our music streaming footprints shape us as listeners

items.title: Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali | Softer Volumes
items.text: Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali | Softer Volumes Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali | Softer Volumes Specialty Coffee Shops in Bali Beautiful cafes and roasteries to visit for your island coffee Bali, renowned for its breathtaking landscapes and cultural richness, has also become a notable destination for specialty coffee. Beyond its allure as a tropical paradise, the island boasts a burgeoning coffee culture characterised by distinctive flavours and innovative cafe designs. From serene establishments tucked amidst verdant rice terraces to sleek urban hubs in bustling locales like Canggu, Bali offers a diverse array of specialty coffee shops that combine aesthetic excellence with exceptional brews. Here we showcase a few of Bali’s best specialty coffee shops, highlighting their unique design elements and the coffee experiences they offer. Discover more coffee shops in our Bali Island Guide . Miel Miel is a bright and airy cafe with high ceilings and plenty of indoor greenery. The coffee offering includes a rotation of blends and single-origin roasts, and the food menu consists of breakfast and lunch classics and delicious pastries. @miel.bali Acme Bakehouse & Coffee Roasters Acme is a bakehouse and coffee roaster with two locations in Canggu. items.text: Macbook Pro with M3 Chip — Elevating Creativity | Softer Volumes Macbook Pro with M3 Chip — Elevating Creativity | Softer Volumes Elevating Creativity Powerful New MacBook Pro with M3 Chip In creative fields, having reliable and powerful tools is crucial for unleashing creativity and swiftly bringing visions to life. Apple recently released the new MacBook Pro lineup featuring the all-new family of M3 chips: M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max. These cutting-edge chips have been meticulously crafted to cater to the unique demands of creative professionals, offering unparalleled performance, exceptional graphics capabilities, and innovative features. Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch M3 Max Performance Crafted for Creatives The M3 chip family introduces three variants, each tailored to elevate the creative experience. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M3 excels not only in everyday tasks but also delivers sustained performance in pro apps and games, making it the perfect companion for photographers, designers, and budding creatives. For those pushing creative boundaries, the M3 Pro models provide enhanced performance and additional unified memory support. Available in a sleek Space Black finish, these models cater to coders, creatives, and researchers who demand more from their tools. For creators seeking the utmost in performance, the M3 Max models redefine computing limits. With a monster GPU, a powerful CPU, and support for up to 128GB of unified memory, these models cater to machine learning programmers, 3D artists, and video editors. Display Brilliance and Connectivity All MacBook Pro models feature a dazzling Liquid Retina XDR display, setting new standards for visual excellence. With 20 percent brighter SDR content, this display provides an immersive canvas for your artistic endeavors. The built-in 1080p camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a variety of connectivity options make the MacBook Pro lineup a perfect blend of form and function, catering to the multifaceted needs of creative professionals. Unmatched Portability and Flexibility In addition to its powerhouse performance, the new MacBook Pro stands out for its impressive portability, catering to the on-the-go needs of creative professionals. The sleek design, coupled with the M3 chip’s efficiency, strikes a perfect balance between power and portability, allowing you to carry your creative studio wherever inspiration strikes. The robust M3 chip not only delivers exceptional performance but also empowers you to work on intensive projects in any environment. Whether you’re on a plane, commuting, working from home, or at a cafe, the MacBook Pro ensures a seamless and efficient creative process. The combination of power and portability allows you to turn any space into your studio, providing flexibility that enhances your productivity and creativity on the go. Empowering creative professionals by seamlessly combining power, innovation, and portability, Apple has created a tool that exceeds the expectations of photographers, designers, coders, and video editors alike. With the M3 Apple MacBook Pro, creative professionals have the freedom to unleash their creativity wherever, whenever, and however inspiration strikes. apple.com Words by Hugo Johnson Photographs by Softer Volumes Softer Volumes: Cafés — Digital Book 290 beautifully-designed cafés around the world, showcased in a premium digital book. items.text: Boca de Agua | Softer Volumes Boca de Agua | Softer Volumes Boca de Agua A sustainable retreat in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula Nearby the crystal clear blue waters of Bacalar Lagoon in Mexico, Boca de Agua , conceived by architect Frida Escobedo , emerges as a harmonious blend of modern design and natural splendour. This architectural gem serves as a retreat where contemporary aesthetics meet sustainable principles, offering a luxurious escape in a jungle paradise. Escobedo’s design ethos is palpable in the hotel’s aesthetic, characterised by its sleek lines and a commitment to utilising locally sourced materials. With a deliberate incorporation of natural elements like wood and stone, the architecture seamlessly integrates with the lush surroundings, creating a symbiotic relationship between the built environment and nature. The hotel’s layout is meticulously designed to provide guests with both tranquillity and privacy. The carefully curated rooms and communal spaces, adorned with minimalist yet sophisticated furnishings, enhance the overall guest experience, inviting a sense of calm and fostering connection. What sets Boca de Agua apart is not just its architectural brilliance but also its dedication to sustainable practices. The incorporation of eco-friendly technologies and a reliance on local craftsmanship exemplify a commitment to responsible tourism. This not only reduces the hotel’s environmental impact but also contributes to a culturally rich experience for guests. As visitors immerse themselves in the serene ambience, Boca de Agua offers a seamless coexistence of luxury and sustainability. Whether indulging in private sanctuaries or communal spaces, each moment at Boca de Agua reflects a fusion of modern elegance, natural beauty, and a deep-rooted commitment to a sustainable and culturally immersive escape. items.text: Innit Lombok Resort Design Hotels | Softer Volumes Innit Lombok Resort Design Hotels | Softer Volumes Secluded Beachfront Sanctuary Innit Lombok is perched on the white-sand shores of Ekas Bay in Lombok, Indonesia Situated in the serene Ekas Bay, Innit Lombok —a member of Design Hotels —is a peaceful beachfront sanctuary encompassed by picturesque landscapes. Boasting a private white-sand beach that stretches 250 metres, this resort provides seven villas that seamlessly blend contemporary design with traditional Indonesian elements. The villas feature open-living spaces on the upper level and expansive dining areas on the beach level. The interiors include teak wood finishes, ironwood decking, and striking facades constructed with wood commonly utilised by local boat builders. At Anakampung restaurant, guests can appreciate artwork by talented Indonesian artists, while the villas themselves draw inspiration from the island’s traditional Lumbung-style houses. The resort also distinguishes itself as a culinary destination. With a Michelin-starred Indonesian chef at the helm, the menu showcases farm-to-table cuisine and locally sourced seafood, offering a truly remarkable dining experience. Innit Lombok presents a rare and unexplored coastal haven, providing seclusion and unparalleled natural beauty for discerning travellers. — Architecture by d-associates architect . W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 The Whiteley, Private Residence, London Taking inspiration from the spirit of a worldly collector, we have crafted a residence within The Whiteley that feels both storied and spontaneous, a home that unfolds like a curated journey across cultures, eras, and materials. This layered approach speaks to a life of travel, taste, and thoughtful accumulation, where each object has a narrative and every surface invites touch. The design balances restraint and exuberance, heritage and modernity, all with a sense of quiet luxury. Balancing historic authenticity with imaginative expression, the space honours the building’s Edwardian roots through bespoke mouldings, architectural panelling, and grand proportions, while introducing playful gestures like custom Fromental wallpaper and bold shifts in volume. The furnishings are drawn from a global palette: Georgian chandeliers, Irish-made pieces from Orior, Parisian prints from Cahiers d’Art, rugs by Pinton and CC Tapis, and bespoke objects by L’OBJET and The Lacquer Company. Together, they create an atmosphere that feels at once elevated and deeply personal. The bedrooms retreat into a softer, more intimate rhythm. The master suite is composed with subtle textures and vintage lighting, while secondary rooms continue the narrative of curated eclecticism with heirloom-inspired furniture and hand-finished details. A mezzanine level, overlooking the main living space, offers a moment of quiet escape, a study, library, or atelier suspended above the heart of the home. items.text: Club Bâtard | Joyce Wang Studio scrollTop: 0px, scrollLeft: 0px --> Skip to content Design Bespoke About Contact En En Cn --> Enquiries General info@joycewangstudio.com New Business info@joycewangstudio.com Press laura@lbagency.co Jobs apply@joycewangstudio.com London 1 Warren Mews London. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Club Bâtard, Private Members Club, Hong Kong Spanning three floors in the historic Pedder Building, the three-story wine cellar for Club Bâtard is the largest of its kind in Asia. A pièce de résistance of a cellar design conceived in collaboration with Sensis World and built to exceptional quality to house the most coveted of wine collections. Aside from storing wine, the space stitches all three floors together, allowing guests to wander freely to select their wines and to finally enjoy it at their tables. ⁠ We want it to be an experience in itself for one to travel through the cellar, each floor with a distinct narrative to celebrate the unique regions and flavours of the grape. ⁠ Located on the first floor, Le Clos pays homage to the ‘clos’, an ode to the cloisters and the origin of wine making as a monastic ritual.. A double-barrelled ceiling reminiscent of religious naves sets a reverent tone, while rustic stone columns and Beaux-Arts flourishes evoke old-world grandeur. Playful custom details like scrolling metalwork, Miró-inspired mosaic tiles, and bespoke chandeliers bring levity to the space. On the second floor, Bâtard reinterprets the classical French brasserie with a warm, contemporary edge. Stood in the centre of the cellar is a jewellery vitrine of wines – a tribute to French haute couture and their famed display cases. Rich materials like burgundy leather, hammered copper, and faceted mirrors, create a sense of intimacy and understated luxury. The dining room flows into a sunlit terrace wrapped in custom wallpaper, where subtle Bâtard motifs playfully hide in plain sight. A mix of elegance and ease, Bâtard is designed for both casual gatherings and more private moments behind sculptural portals in its secluded dining rooms. Tucked away like a secret library of spirits, OBE is the club’s whisky bar located on the third floor. Named after the “Old Bottle Effect”, a term referring to the complex character that evolves in aged whiskies. Designed as an intimate and enveloping refuge, OBE is anchored by a curved, custom-built floor-to-ceiling cabinet clad in lustrous anodised black metal, housing an extensive collection with a focus on rare Japanese labels. The ambience is low-lit and contemplative, with soft wall sconces, table lamps and plush black leather banquettes creating a cocoon of calm sophistication where one can sip and savour undisturbed. Also located on the uppermost floor, Hop Sze is a contemporary Chinese restaurant inspired by the original namesake in Sai Wan Ho. The design breathes lightness and vitality into the space, with lantern-like light fixtures, abstracted Chinese joinery, and bold yet elegant contrasts in marble, wood and textile. Pops of colour and playfully reinterpreted signage elements bring a youthful spirit to the interiors, while private dining rooms and expansive views offer a refined, elevated setting for both intimate and celebratory gatherings. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 Prince and the Peacock, Hong Kong As the second phase of The Magistracy in Hong Kong, a historic judicial house which has been sensitively reimagined and restored by Black Sheep Hospitality Group in Hong Kong. Featuring a 60-seat main dining space, alongside two unique private dining rooms, and a sports lounge named Jack’s Racquet Room. The spaces are inspired by the rich cultural impact and patronage of the Maharajas, Maharanis, Nawabs, Nizams and Emperors who ruled India’s diverse patchwork of territories before, during and after the colonial era. Just as the country’s aristocrats and monarchs developed intertwined food and artistic cultures, the design of Prince and the Peacock is designed to meld effortlessly with the aromas and flavours of the cuisine created by Chef Palash Mitra of New Punjab Club in Hong Kong, the world’s only Punjabi restaurant with a Michelin star. An invocation of the opulence of historic royal palaces and courts, the peacock takes centre stage in a subtle blend of motifs and vibrant colours inspired by the legendary bird, which still serves as India’s icon of royalty and power. Adjacent to the balcony space hang traditional punkah fans, reminiscent of palatial interiors where the fanning of fresh air was a regal requirement. The Magistracy has been expanded with two private dining room options on the second floor. The first, named the Ruby Room, is designed to host groups of up to 8 people and has been artfully decorated in scarlet tones with a stunning tiled ceiling. The second space, The Kohinoor, was named after one of the world’s largest cut diamonds and holds up to 8 in a room resplendent with elegant pink ceiling drapery. ” This lounge and bar space blends the classic elegance of South Asian sports clubs, with the comfort and sophistication of everything you’d expect from a modern hospitality setting. The space features rich, dark rosewood timber, recalling clubrooms of old, while the lounge area exudes plush comfort with mohair, velvets, and leather armchairs, creating an inviting and luxurious atmosphere. The colour palette is inspired by traditional sports, found in the deep red of cricket balls, warm mustard tones, fresh lime green, and the orange hues of red travertine, as well as striped fabrics drawing on classic club jersey styles.” -Joyce Wang Jack Racquet’s Room blends the classic elegance of South Asian sports clubs with the comfort and sophistication of everything you’d expect from a modern hospitality setting. items.text: THE MAGARIGAWA CLUB Clubhouse | Joyce Wang Studio scrollTop: 0px, scrollLeft: 0px --> Skip to content Design Bespoke About Contact En En Cn --> Enquiries General info@joycewangstudio.com New Business info@joycewangstudio.com Press laura@lbagency.co Jobs apply@joycewangstudio.com London 1 Warren Mews London. W1T 6AJ T +44(0)20 7436 8846 Hong Kong Ground Floor 12 Kennedy Street Wan Chai Hong Kong T +852 2804 1138 THE MAGARIGAWA CLUB Clubhouse, Japan Set high in the forested hills of Chiba, Japan, THE MAGARIGAWA CLUB is designed as a retreat for driving enthusiasts. Anchoring a 2.2-mile private driving course, the Clubhouse reimagines the traditional race facility as a resort-style destination. Inspired by the refined minimalism of Japanese design, the space unfolds in layers of timber, stone, and soft light, framing panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and track. Every detail is considered, not only for the driver, but for the community that comes with them. At the heart of Magarigawa’s private driving course lies the 18-bay pit lane, designed to merge your garage with a lounge space, where performance and pause coexist. Seating lines the bays, allowing members to hang out right beside their vehicles. We wanted the space to feel like an extension of your supercar, equipped with state-of-the-art tech, authentic finishes, and ergonomic seating. A place where you can host friends, spend time with family, and connect with like-minded individuals who share a passion for the track. Play Pause Sound: on Sound: off Shoji screens play a central role in shaping the clubhouse experience. Rather than serving as fixed dividers, they offer a flexible way to define space, softening light, creating privacy, and guiding movement without disrupting visual continuity. Custom-built for the project, the screens are crafted from natural timber and layered paper, allowing them to subtly shift the atmosphere throughout the day. Their presence reinforces the connection to traditional Japanese interiors, while serving a distinctly modern function within the architecture. The clubhouse offers a full range of amenities for members and their guests. These include an outdoor infinity pool, a wellness centre with onsen, restaurant, kids’ club, wine and cigar bar, and multiple dining and lounge areas. Members also have access to 9 private villas, each with panoramic track views and direct connections to clubhouse facilities. The overall experience is designed to be immersive and complete, a destination for drivers and their families alike. items.title: AP House Miami - Studio Dado
items.text: AP House Miami The perfect blend of space and timelessness Featured Project AUDEMARS PIGUET HOUSE MIAMI In Miami, time bends to the beat of the city. There’s a rhythm here. A syncopation of light, water, and movement that slows you down just enough to notice the details. Studio DADO infused AP House Miami with this energy. All at once, it’s a boutique, a showroom, a workplace and a museum. It’s a series of moments strung like pearls on an elegant necklace: every one intentional, luminescent and unique; every one designed to make you feel something glorious. Our goal wasn’t just to create a space, but to create a choreography of sensations, from entry to terrace, bar to lounge, watch display to custom studio. And every detail speaks to the Audemars Piguet brand and the soul of Miami. The design celebrates the wonder of time, built on legacy and craftsmanship, finding stillness in luxury and discovering a sense of self in the process. Next Project Ocean Blue

items.title: Allura Vista Suite - Studio Dado
items.text: Allura Vista Suite A personal touch in a home away from home Guestrooms & Suites Allura Vista Suite Studio DADO reimagined the meaning of luxury with the Vista Suite on Oceania Cruises Allura , a space that feels as natural and considered as a true home at sea. Every gesture, material, and proportion is guided by emotion and experience. The vestibule sets an understated tone before opening into a light-filled living area defined by marble-wrapped walls, bespoke furniture, and a floating bar that feels both sculptural and inviting. The bedroom flows seamlessly into a dressing area that encourages ease and movement, while the bathroom becomes a private sanctuary with its marble soaking tub, generous vanity, and integrated storage. Every detail, from the sweep of the ceiling to the quiet texture of wood and leather, reflects care and craftsmanship. The result is an environment that feels effortless, personal, and distinctly human. Next Project Vista Penthouse Suite

items.title: Serene Spa and Wellness - Studio Dado
items.text: Serene Spa and Wellness Unwind in a multi-sensory experience, designed to help guests relax at every turn. Spa & Fitness In Seven Seas Grandeur’s spa, the floral motif carries through the space, offering a visual reminder of rebirth and rejuvenation. The corridor leading to the reception desk is a processional experience, filled with architectural details like articulated metal canopies and lantern niches that set the scene. In the salon, a scalloped effect echoes the sea without relying on a heavy-handed theme. The treatment rooms have a rich and inviting look that feels like a cocoon while the relaxation room offers a sense of privacy and enchantment, as though guests are inside a topiary maze. Outside, three Jacuzzis and a lounge area offer private views of the sea in a warm, welcoming space that is the perfect counterpoint to the fresh sea air. Next Project Aquamar Spa and Wellness

items.title: Grand Atrium - Studio Dado
items.text: Grand Atrium A dazzling first impression for a deeply luxurious ship. Public Spaces Gentle curves ease the mind As the first space guests encounter when boarding Oceania Vista , the Grand Atrium sets the emotional tone for the journey ahead. More than a point of entry, it offers a moment of calm and clarity. Inspired by the organic spiral of a nautilus shell, the layout flows with gentle curves and open sightlines that guide the body and ease the mind. The central lighting column spirals downward in a soft, continuous gesture, echoing the shell’s inner chambers and creating a processional path that draws guests into the heart of the ship. Wall paneling mirrors this motion in sections, adding depth and movement without distraction. Texture, form and light take the lead The marine inspiration continues in the space’s most captivating feature: a custom floor-to-ceiling chandelier. Suspended in motion, it evokes a swirling vortex of water or a school of fish gliding through the current. Beneath it, herringbone tilework with gold accents catches the light in a way that recalls the iridescent shimmer found inside a seashell. The material palette is intentionally restrained, allowing texture, form, and light to take the lead. Although the architecture is undeniably grand, transitional furnishings soften the space, introducing a residential comfort that makes the arrival feel personal and grounded. Next Project Grand Bar

items.title: Magnus Ström Architects Practice in Hampshire, New Forest, UK - Strom Architects | Ström Architects
items.text: Home link Studio At the age of five, Magnus Ström wanted to be an architect. Growing up in Sweden, he was immersed in a design culture that believed function and beauty are not in competition, that knowing what to remove matters as much as knowing what to keep, and that the natural world belongs inside as much as out. The best buildings, in that tradition, earn their presence rather than perform it. Good architecture should feel inevitable, not designed, but revealed. The best spaces we have made are the ones where we relentlessly edited until what remained was exactly right, nothing added for effect, nothing kept out of habit. When it works, you walk into a room and feel it before you can explain it. This accumulative effect is what Magnus refers to as the "je ne sais quoi" of buildings, with the result so particular to its owners and its site that it could not have been built anywhere else for anyone else. Magnus has always gravitated towards the sea and the horizon, and the practice's work reflects that - framing views, connecting inside to out, putting people in direct contact with their environment. We design bespoke private houses, multi-residential developments, and high-end hospitality projects including spas and resorts. Most of our clients engage a full Architecture and Interior Design Service. Our studios in England and the Turks and Caicos Islands, Caribbean, service work across Europe, the Americas, and the Middle East. We take on a limited number of the right projects each year. We choose our clients as carefully as they choose us. The relationship has to be built on trust and genuine creative alignment. When it is, the results tend to be something neither party could have arrived at alone. Working across different planning systems, construction cultures and climates has given the practice a practical fluency that a domestically focused architect cannot offer. We know how projects get built in different parts of the world, and we manage that on behalf of clients. Every commission gets consistent attention from senior people throughout. Magnus leads design across the practice, Nicky Jones manages operations as Managing Director, and Kyle Barclay leads the Turks and Caicos Islands studio as its co-founder. Hugh Richardson leads technical delivery as Technical Director. Together with our team of architects and associates, we cover every stage from the first conversation to completion. The goal is always the same: a building that improves the life lived inside it. div; cls: uk-animation-fade; uk-animation-fast; delay: 0; repeat: true"> 1. Track Record The portfolio is the place to start. What it demonstrates is not just a visual identity but a depth of thinking that transfers across typologies, climates and contexts. A practice that has resolved complex briefs across multiple countries and building types brings that accumulated problem-solving to every new commission, including ones it has not encountered before. 2. We understand how you live Every client we work with has a particular way of living. We find that out early, and build everything from it. The brief is not just about rooms and square footage - it is about how someone moves through a day, what they need a building to do for them, and what they want to feel when they are in it. Most clients engage us for architecture and interior design together. That integration is not a service add-on - it is how the most considered spaces get made, with every decision in the building serving the same intention. 3. We straighten the process Time is the one thing clients cannot recover. We handle complexity so that clients do not have to: identifying risks before they become problems, resolving decisions before they reach site, and maintaining cost clarity throughout. The goal is a process that demands as little of the client as possible while delivering as much as the project is capable of. items.title: Vero's Art Process — Studio Vero / Veronica Buda
items.text: My Process I use digital photography to showcase the existing beauty of our world that surrounds us, brings us joy and helps us heal. Through landscape, storytelling and micro photography, I try to tell stories about our life, our environment, and bring some of the smallest and most intricate details to the light. I also use staging to imagine stories and to raise awareness on various social and individual matters. I usually imagine a story and find the objects I could use to express it, but sometimes objects tell me a story, and I listen. I use abstract acrylic painting to bring ideas and emotions into life. My sources of inspiration are generated from nature, spirituality, traditions, and everyday life, but I usually prefer to not paint what I can photograph. I love working with spirals and circles and I often like to give my paintings more than one title. Currently, my style is clean and structured. The dynamics or tensions are generated by the forms, shapes and color transitions rather than by brush strokes or textures. I like to paint on medium to large size canvases so I have the freedom of expression. I usually begin with an image or a story in my head and I sketch it in pencil. When the design is ready, I transfer it to canvas, and start painting until I am satisfied with the result or when something inside tells me to stop. I like to mix my own colors and I prefer not to use them straight from the tube. I also use professional grade paints and materials. In both photography and painting, I use sacred geometry and I try to capture and include fractals whenever the opportunity arises. I do this with the purpose of bringing a sense of balance to the composition and tranquility to the viewer. To highlight the importance of recycling, I buy used / vintage frames and I give them a new life by upcycling and using them to compliment my framed artwork. I cut my own mat board so I can have the flexibility of choosing the best suitable color for the piece I frame. I use acid free professional grade materials except in cases when I reuse the materials that came with a vintage frame. If I am not sure of their provenience I mention it in the product description.

items.title: DIY Porch Swing: Step-by-Step Plans and Build Guide - Parts And Labor Design
items.text: DIY Porch Swing: Step-by-Step Plans and Build Guide - Parts And Labor Design Skip to content DIY Porch Swing: Step-by-Step Plans and Build Guide Outdoor Design ON September 22, 2026 BY Brighton Davis Written By Brighton Davis Brighton covers outdoor and landscape design at Parts and Labor Design. Before writing, he spent six years in landscape installation, building patios, gardens, and backyards for every kind of budget. About Author Edited By Leslie Royce Leslie is the managing editor at Parts and Labor Design. She studied interior design before moving into editorial work, and reads every piece before it’s published. Table of Content A DIY porch swing does not need complicated joinery to feel solid and safe. It needs a square base, clean joints, and hanging hardware sized for the structure above it, in that order. This is a standard bench-style swing, not an oversized swing bed, and it is realistic for one person working alone. I’d put the difficulty at a 3 out of 5, the build time around 6 hours for the bench itself, and the materials cost at about $100 or more before cushion or finish. The two things that actually derail this build are an out-of-square base and hanging hardware that outmatches the structure it is screwed into. Difficulty 3 of 5, straightforward joinery, but square framing and load-rated hanging hardware raise the stakes Time About 6 hours for the bench itself, plus separate time for finish curing and installation Cost Around $100 and up in lumber and hardware, excluding cushion and finish Tools Needed Miter or circular saw, drill, framing square, clamps, tape measure, pencil, sander Skill Required Beginner to intermediate Treat the cost as a starting point rather than a fixed budget. Lumber prices, exterior finish, and mounting hardware account for most of the swing. If you’re not sure this style fits your space, it helps to look at compact porch layouts before you buy any lumber. The Most Common Way This Build Goes Wrong Most porch swing problems trace back to one of two moments. The first is a base that goes together slightly out of square, which the back and arms will amplify rather than hide. The second is hanging the finished swing from something that was never meant to carry a swinging load, like a soffit board or a section of trim. Catch the first one with a square and a diagonal check before you drive a single screw. Catch the second one before you buy any lumber at all, by confirming what is actually above your porch ceiling. The same failure point shows up in other outdoor structures, too. Framing a treehouse platform runs into the identical issue: hardware only performs as well as the wood it’s anchored to. Porch Swing Plan and Measurements The base uses 57 1/2 inch front and rear rails with 21-inch end pieces and internal supports . The heavier base pieces come from 2×6 lumber, while the backrest, side rails, arm supports, and remaining framing use 2×4 boards. The plan also calls for 48 1/2 inch structural rails, 27 inch side components, 28 1/2 inch armrests, and a 55 1/2 inch upper back rail. Cut matching pieces from the same measurements rather than sizing one side on its own. That gives the two arms, side rails, and repeated supports a real chance of lining up during assembly. If you want to widen the swing, revise the related rails and support spacing together, since extending a single board throws the rest of the frame out of proportion. Materials and Cut List For the main frame, prepare two 2x6x8 boards and six 2x4x8 boards .
