Large, elegant, fluted columns in the middle of the dining room are crowned with curved, ribbed glowing resin, and add an Art Deco glamour to the dining room. No items found. No items found. "A modern Korean steakhouse shimmers in Dallas." A large feature fireplace clad in blood-red stone warms the room. Opposite, an AvroKO-designed, brass metal and mirror illuminated installation is layered in front of a hand-painted DeGournay wall covering of ancient dwarf trees and iridescent gold, adding both elegance and sparkle to the room. The large AvroKO-designed chandeliers hanging below a solid brass tiled reflective ceiling cove are inspired by the largest of heat sinks, with radiating fins made of brass that surround a glowing core. Hanging beads and reflective surfaces add a decorative softness to an otherwise gritty mechanically-inspired design. The Member’s Room offers private access to exclusive and rare spirits, special tasting menus, and unique programming. items.text: Doha , Qatar La Méditerannée Restaurant , Est. Doha , Qatar Restaurant , Est. About La Méditerranée Robuchon at the Four Seasons Resort and Residences at The Pearl-Qatar is a luxurious French seafood restaurant inspired by the Mediterranean, where guests are immersed in a space of bohemian elegance and the fantastical sea. Freshness is key to the restaurant, from the ingredients served to the space guests dine—transporting them into a space of unexpected delight. Supper "French refinement meets the mystique of the deep sea." LOCATION Doha , Qatar Size 8,234 ft² / 765 m² CaTEGORY Food & Beverage Client Four Seasons Keys A Curated Experience Dining at its finest As guests enter, a display of fresh seafood on ice with live lobsters in the aquarium below, lets guests select their choices before the chef takes them away for preparation. Guests can see their food being prepared from the moment they arrive, allowing them to participate in the theatre of the restaurant. The back bar showcases a full range of wines, oils, and limited liquors. Open Gallery From dishes to drinks, a guest's experience is meant to be specific to each individual. Oceanic Inspiration The main dining room recalls scenes from the sea. Banquettes call to mind ocean coral, with organic forms avoiding anything linear. A range of bespoke dining and bar stools draw on shell forms, upholstered in coral reds and shades of teal. Custom-made drink carts and champagne trollies were designed to meet the need of operations to be empowered to create curated and significant experiences for their guests. No items found. Hanging fabric panels add a lightness and intimacy allowing movement from the sea breeze. These pieces often define the spaces they are placed in. ​ Designed in the UK, the Editions are hand-made by some of the finest artisans, focusing on materials, texture and details. ​ Contact us for more information CH05 Listening Chair Armchair for vinyl turntable and record collection. Upholstered in ‘Dedar Splendido Splendente’ metallic silk velvet. Fabric of your choice available (COM). Shown in Oak. Also available in Ebonised oak. 40 dia x 52 H cm Also available as a bar stool. ​ ​ __ Learn about this piece SO02 Sofa Faceted modular sofa with hole detail at back. Designed and crafted in the UK using traditional upholstery methods. Upholstered in ‘Dedar Monsieur Baudelaire’ cotton velvet. Cushions double sided in ‘Dedar Patchwork’, ‘Dedar Adorabile Alpaca’ and tufted braid. Fabric of your choice available (COM). items.title: Publication — Rockwell Group
items.text: Books Our design philosophy and approach has been distilled into recurring narrative arcs, explorations, and areas of interest. Drama A definitive collection of Rockwell Group’s work and a compelling manifesto for multi-disciplinary collaboration. Drama distills the magic inherent in both theater and architecture and encourages us to look at creativity in a more personal, human-centered way. Buy the Book More Information What If...? What if you could step inside a crystal goblet? What if your environment transformed with every step? What if a restaurant could vanish at a moment’s notice? What If…? presents a wide array of David Rockwell’s explorations of the rich intersection between architecture and theater. Buy the Book More Information Spectacle With Spectacle , designers David Rockwell and Bruce Mau present a dynamic visual essay that celebrates the phenomenon and history of communal, awe-inspiring public performance worldwide: from the stadium to the streets, from religious festivals to political marches, and from the ever-changing skyline of Las Vegas to ephemeral fireworks displays. Buy the Book More Information Pleasure Pleasure is the first book to showcase the hotels, theaters, restaurants, stadiums, casinos and other public spaces created by Rockwell Group. items.title: The Bellagio - Las Vegas, Nevada — Champalimaud Design
items.text: The Bellagio LAS VEGAS, NEVADA The Bellagio embodies the transformative quality of Las Vegas, taking us out of the ordinary to a different place and time. Our studio renovated the Spa Tower Suites to create a residential aesthetic with the timeless elegance that is unique to the property. We found rich inspiration in the colors of Lake Como's surrounding flora and the classical style of the building's architecture. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize A residential aesthetic with the timeless elegance that is uniquely Bellagio. The refreshed Spa Tower Suites are relaxed and residential in feeling, with a subtle play of color. Guests are enveloped in neutral hues punctuated by colorful custom furnishings and accent pieces, each inspired by a vision of Northern Italy, past and present. The bespoke and sophisticated touches extend to folding screens painted with moody landscapes, works of plaster bas relief, and wallcoverings inspired by traditional Italian craft paper. We found inspiration in the colors of Lake Como's surrounding flora and the classical style of the building's architecture. The expression of an artful, subtle elegance. An art selection featuring abstract expressionist painting imbues the new spaces with a fresh contemporary edge. There is a contrast among the suites between their sharp, tailored style, and the effortlessly comfortable experience of staying in them. As the notion of luxury continues to evolve across hospitality, this project aims to progress its evolution in Las Vegas through an emphasis on nature, and the expression of an artful, subtle elegance. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Back to Resorts & Hotels

items.title: 77 Peak Road - Hong Kong — Champalimaud Design
items.text: 77 Peak Road HONG KONG 77 Peak Road is tucked away on a breathtaking hillside of Hong Kong’s prestigious Victoria Peak. The villas are enveloped with lush forest greenery, offering the rarity of privacy and seclusion. Through Champalimaud’s timeless sensitivity to detail, 77 Peak captivates with a strong sensibility towards design and an appreciation of the opulent lifestyle. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Enveloped with lush forest greenery. Upon entry, the architectural impact of the wood screens and cascading X-meter glass chandelier furthers the grandeur with an immediate sense of arrival. Beyond the distinct wooden framework, the elegant living, dining and library spaces provide an intuitive balance between intimate and formal settings. For family living, a kitchen equipped with cutting-edge appliances and seamless design details serves as an effortless retreat from the fast pace of life in Hong Kong. A balance between an intimate and formal setting An effortless retreat. Champalimaud’s carefully considered use of rare marbles, dramatic chandeliers, tailored draperies, handcrafted millwork and elaborate stone floors defines the epitome of finely considered, modern living. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Back to Private Homes

items.title: Raffles Hotel - Singapore — Champalimaud Design
items.text: Raffles Hotel SINGAPORE Crowned as one of the greatest hotels in the world, the interiors of the Raffles Singapore represent a delicate layering of modernity, authenticity, and refined beauty, with a meticulous attention to detail. Champalimaud refreshed the design direction of this iconic hotel, drawing out its essence through honest creative decisions and poetic detail. Maintaining the ambience and sense of place that the property is known for, the spirit of Raffles is awakened through bold and effectual design. It’s a memory of old Singapore revitalized with a contemporary and artful approach. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize The past, through a present lens. As a national monument, special attention was paid to the preservation of the original colonial architecture. Public spaces have been re-planned to cultivate social engagement and create an ease of flow between spaces. With a sensibility that is much more contemporary than its previous design iterations, we emphasized scale through a curation of sumptuously shaped custom furniture, ornate screens, locally sourced heritage antiques, and impactful lighting. Sumptuous shapes, ornate screens, locally sourced heritage antiques, and impactful lighting. The palette is composed of the original black and white contrasts juxtaposed with caramel, shades of green, and creamy neutrals. The new reception and lobby lounge, once iconic places frequented by dignitaries and diplomats, is transformed into an elegant reception that serves as the gateway to the hotel’s alluring spaces for dining and imbibing: The Tiffin Room, The Writer’s Bar, La Dame de Pic, Long Bar, and Butcher’s Block. The palette is composed of the original black and white contrasts juxtaposed with caramel, shades of green, and creamy neutrals. Light floral references and gilded trimming along with a bejeweled chandelier add a layer of refinement to the overall vision. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Back to Resorts & Hotels

items.title: The Emory - London, United Kingdom — Champalimaud Design
items.text: The Emory LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM The Emory is a classically inspired, contemporary nod to the London lifestyle. It is about creating ease of living presented in a beautiful way, with a bespoke spirit. Our suites were inspired by London’s forward-thinking urbanism and the ideal that elevated design can coexist with a streamlined aesthetic. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Ease of living presented in a beautiful way. We hoped to make the experience of each space intuitive and uplifting. Following an entrance moment looking down the suite onto Hyde Park, a door is closed to create a private moment at the backlit vanity. There is a contemporary urbanism to the space, a sense that you will find sanctuary from the bustle of the city. The serene rooms are quietly elevated by a cladding of wood panels in bleached black limba and a herringbone wood floor. There is a contemporary urbanism to the space, a sense that you will find sanctuary from the bustle of the city. Calming and artful with a unified design. Ultimately, our idea was to create a room which is calming and artful with a unified design. Though contemporary in context and in an urban environment, the suite plays the role of a respite, full of warmth and without cold colors. Sculptural and artistic in their sensibility, the design elements have been choreographed to stand together as gallery pieces. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Back to Resorts & Hotels

items.title: The Pearl Lounge - Bahrain — Champalimaud Design
items.text: The Pearl Lounge BAHRAIN The Pearl Lounge was created as an intimate platform for Bahraini hospitality to shine. We applied traditional concepts of Arabic hospitality to a series of spaces built around hospitality gestures, like the café, the bar, and the a la carte restaurants. It is a promenade of indulgences where each space has its own mood, its own speed, and its own offerings for guests. There are quiet places, loud places, formal dining rooms, and spaces to just hang around and work while having a drink. We deconstructed the typical open plan found in many lounges into discrete rooms, each containing unique guest offerings. The concept is a promenade of indulgences. By taking cues from our hotel and high-end residential design experience, we translated the impact of intimate spaces to the travel lounge setting. Because the scale of these spaces is more familiar and intimate, it becomes easier to host a guest, and to tell a story. A signature gesture used throughout the Lounge is the portal , or large framed opening. This element defines both the end of one space and the entry to another. When scaled correctly, it helps the lounge feel both intimate and grand at the same time. The Pearl Lounge would not present itself as one sprawling space, but as a series of unique environments focused on customer service and choice. A fine balance emerges between personal and shared space. We put an emphasis on understanding how one lives and ultimately uses a space. In the Pearl Lounge, a fine balance emerges between personal and shared space. A guest wants to feel as if they are sitting in the best seat in the house no matter which seat in the lounge they choose to settle. Back to Food & Beverage

items.title: The Centrale - New York, New York — Champalimaud Design
items.text: The Centrale NEW YORK, NEW YORK The Centrale possesses a distinct street level presence, the perforated screen on its front façade creating a sense of enclosure while letting light flow through. Our studio strived to emulate this subtle drama throughout the interior design. The Lobby complements the exterior façade with high slated ceilings, large architectural windows, stepped marble features, and a stunning plaster bas relief feature wall with a floral naturescape. Custom artwork, distinctive marbles, natural stones and dramatic light fixtures come together to create an ethereal, intimate feel. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize A tailored and welcoming retreat. Amenities spaces are brought down to a human scale through inspired design moments. We conceived the spaces as an extension to the residents’ own homes—a tailored and welcoming retreat from the outside world. As residents enter The Great Room, they are met with a beautiful double height bespoke ceramic installation by Pascal Girardin, which hangs from a soaring 10-meter ceiling. It is a place bathed in light where residents can relax and unwind. A place bathed in light where residents can relax and unwind. The epitome of luxurious, modern living in New York City. Champalimaud’s curated use of materials from rare marbles, dramatic chandeliers, handcrafted millwork and elaborate stone floors in the design scheme defines the epitome of luxurious, modern living in New York City. items.title: ARTFUL DETAILS — REUNION
items.text: ARTFUL DETAILS Grand experiences are made from small moments. We are passionate about infusing architectural spaces and products with distinct personalities, weaving narrative into even the smallest details of a project. We build ‘real-world sets’ by bringing together illustrators, fine artists, millworkers, and other experts. We employ our love of history, materials, color and craftsmanship to add a depth to every project we work on. items.title: Hotel Clermont — REUNION
items.text: HOTEL CLERMONT Marking the revitalization of a legendary Southern landmark, Hotel Clermont has reopened in Poncey-Highland neighborhood as a 94-room boutique hotel drenched in local history and culture Reunion Goods & Services designed the hotel, including its Viennese inspired brasserie Tiny Lou’s, lobby bar and rooftop. Architecture firm Gamble + Gamble restored the iconic building with a focus on historic preservation and revitalization. Reunion enlisted Atlanta wonderkinds Office of Brothers to develop the property’s incredible identity system and collateral. And not to worry, the beloved Clermont Lounge remains untouched in the hotel’s basement. CLIENT Oliver Hospitality LOCATION Atlanta, GA WEBSITE hotelclermont.com GOODS AND SERVICES Interior Architecture Interior Design Creative Direction

items.title: Osborne Residence — REUNION
items.text: OBSBORNE RESIDENCE Completed in 1885 and catty-corner to Carnegie Hall, The Osborne at 205 W 57th Street is considered one of the great apartment buildings of New York City. Reunion Goods & Services , in collaboration with architects Fogarty Finger Architecture, modernized a 2,700 square, 3 bedroom/3 bath apartment while highlighting and restoring the classic details. Designed for a family with two young children, Reunion helped the clients achieve their goal of making the apartment sophisticated and chic, while remaining inviting and comfortable. Reunion used rich fabrics such as boiled wools and velvets to add pops of color and sourced much of the furniture from contemporary up-and-coming designers. The blue cage Nour Lamp by French artist Julie Pfligersdorffer was one of an edition of twelve and several wall coverings were made by Cavern . Artwork includes a gorgeously saturated photograph in the living room by Eric Cahan from his ‘Sky Series’ and a mural by Rebekah Maysles . CLIENT Private Residence LOCATION New York, NY GOODS AND SERVICES Creative Direction Interior Design

items.title: Pinewood Social — REUNION
items.text: PINEWOOD SOCIAL Nashville’s perennial hangout, Pinewood Social combines award-winning cooking, pioneering mixology, the city’s best coffee and bowling under one wood-beamed roof. Reunion Goods & Services was tapped to creative direct the design—conceptualizing artistic moments that imbue the space with the personality of historic athletic and social clubs and helping steer the visual vocabulary. Principal collaborators on the project were Landy Gardner Interiors and Manuel Zeitlin Architects . CLIENT Strategic Hospitality LOCATION Nashville, TN WEBSITE pinewoodsocial.com GOODS AND SERVICES Creative Direction Interior Design Vintage Sourcing Dining tables built from reclaimed lanes, each painted with a stripe of Pinewood's signature color.

items.title: Landmark West Loop — REUNION
items.text: LANDMARK WEST LOOP Landmark West Loop is a ground-up building in Chicago’s West Loop designed by Morris Adjmi. Reunion was brought in to design the building’s 12,000 square feet of common and amenity spaces, as well as to create a complementary identity. Reunion named the property, designed its modular logo and a created a typographic system used across signage, website and marketing. items.text: Stay — Stokes Architecture & Design Menu Jessup House *in collaboration with BLTA and Studios Architecture Stokes was hired to design the interiors of this ground-up mixed-use residential building in Fishtown. Celebrating the post-tension concrete structure of the space, Stokes sought to create interiors that felt modern and industrial while still feeling warm and inviting WORK: -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Spring 2024 WEBSITE: https://livejessuphouse.com/ *photo credits: Jason Varney The Rally *in collaboration with SGRA Stokes was hired to design the interiors of this ground-up mixed-use residential building in Fishtown. The industrial exterior, designed by SGRA, fits perfectly in the context of the working-class neighborhood, while the interior reflects the soul of 70s southern California surf and motorcycle culture. WORK: -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Fall 2023 WEBSITE: https://www.therallyphl.com/ *photo credits: Jason Varney The Pridwin The Pridwin Hotel and Cottages is a classic American resort hotel that has been offering welcoming hospitality on Shelter Island since 1927. The nearly 8 acre site on Crescent Beach was selected for its refreshing breezes and breathtaking water views of the Peconic Bay. The Pridwin has just completed a two year top-to-bottom renovation; maintaining it's classic, timeless traditions, while seamlessly integrating luxury amenities, service and programming for all generations. WORK: -architecture LOCATION: Shelter Island, NY COMPLETED: Summer 2022 WEBSITE: https://www.caperesorts.com/pridwin/ The Quoin Since 1885 the historic Security Trust and Safe Deposit Building has been reborn many times. Listed on the historic register, and originally designed by Philadelphia architect Frank Furness, The Quoin’s exterior remains untouched, while its interior has undergone a complete renovation and redesign by Philadelphia’s Stokes Architecture + Design. Starting down below, the cellar’s cocktail bar, Simmer Down, is mysterious and moody with its original vaulted brick ceiling, curved bar, and lounge seating marked by bookshelves and custom murals by Reverend Michael Allen. Moving up to the lobby, light is invited in through custom art glass windows by Greg Stefan. A herringbone wooden floor purposefully contrasts the wood grid ceiling made of cane. Sinking into plush seating beside the salvaged fireplace and custom-built haberdashery cabinet, guests may enjoy coffee from the bar or at its counter seats. The first floor also houses a 100-seat restaurant and bar, with an open kitchen with a wood-burning oven and grill. Custom and original salvaged pieces come together in a polished look into the building’s past: custom green tiled columns connected by art glass nod to classic banking hues and elements; oak flooring was added to reflect the light streaming from the salvaged laylight that references the buildings original skylight; a new patio was added for seasonal outdoor dining and a view of the Delaware Historic Society gardens. For a daytime view of city or a drink during sunset, guests may head to the brand-new rooftop, intentionally tucked behind the existing mansard roof so it is not visible from the street (as to not change the exterior because it’s part of the historic register). The roof deck overlooks the Delaware Historic Society courtyard. The interior lounge features a bar, and a second fireplace. items.title: Play — Stokes Architecture & Design
items.text: Play — Stokes Architecture & Design Menu City Fitness City Fitness in Fishtown was Stokes' first venture into the realm of physical fitness design. This location, on the ever-developing Frankford Ave. was another example of repurposing beautiful, industrial buildings by embracing their existing character and inserting architectural elements. The space combined 2 buildings, via a wall breach, and added a new second floor space atop the Frankford-adjacent building. In accordance with the developer's vision for Frankford Ave., the façade at the street was opened up, with glass overhead doors and large windows. These openings put on display the juice-bar and gym check-in, an origami-like sculptural object made up of 63 uniquely shaped plywood panels assembled on site. Beyond the check-in desk, a new glass ceiling bridges the gap between buildings, and gives natural sunlight to a live tree. The rear of the building, with its airy wood truss ceiling, acts as the main fitness floor. A mezzanine was added, bringing guests closer to the El Train that roars past the gym on the Front Street side. The second floor addition, with its floor to ceiling glass outer walls, gives full views of Philadelphia and Fishtown. LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Spring 2017 WEBSITE: http://fishtown.cityfitnessphilly.com/ *photo credits: Matt Wargo Pinsetters Bar & Bowl For Pinsetter Bar and Bowl, the client wished to renovate his bowling alley with a few stipulations. The doo-wop style from the previous renovation was to be swapped for a more modern but rustic feel, and the bar and restaurant was to be acoustically insulated from the obvious noise of the bowling alley. Stokes’ strategy was to add a few simple built elements to reinforce some spatial ideas. A lower wood slat ceiling over the entrance created a more welcoming and deliberate entry way and walk-up to the check-in desk, and new walls were built with custom double hung windows to enclose the bar while keeping it visually open. The interior was then completely refinished with cork, reclaimed wood, painted plaster, and a few custom designed elements like booths and a bar soffit. LOCATION: Pennsauken, NJ COMPLETED: Spring 2014 *photo credits: Matt Wargo Morey's Piers Morey’s Piers, located on the boardwalk in Wildwood, consists of three amusement piers and two water parks. It is considered the largest oceanfront amusement complex in the world, and is one of the top ten most visited amusement parks in the country. In an ongoing collaboration with owner Jack Morey, Stokes Architecture designed a collection of large, playful signage, as well as an entry arch evocative of the carnival-like environment of the Pier. LOCATION: Wildwood, NJ WEBSITE: WWW.MOREYSPIERS.COM Ocean Oasis Stokes Architecture collaborated with Jack Morey in transforming an existing water park into more of a resort destination, the Ocean Oasis Beach Club and Water park. The new water park was given a tropical theme, utilizing peeled eucalyptus, bamboo and other natural materials. An existing hot tub was transformed into a grotto with a swim-up bar. An underutilized area under a coaster was transformed with the addition of tiki style cabanas, extensive landscaping, and a fire-pit. A new bar and grille were constructed overlooking the ocean, and a large indoor ticketing facility was built at the entrance. A small Airstream trailer was utilized for a massage cabana. LOCATION: Wildwood, NJ WEBSITE: WWW.MOREYSPIERS.COM prev / next Back to Play 11 City Fitness 5 Pinsetters Bar & Bowl 5 Morey's Piers 4 Ocean Oasis 1700 Sansom Street | Philadelphia, PA19103 | (215)523-9190 | info@stokesarch.com FACEBOOK - INSTAGRAM

items.text: Eat — Stokes Architecture & Design Menu Banshee An Aalto inspired restaurant in Philadelphia WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Winter 2025 website: https://www.bansheephl.com/ *photo credits: Jason Varney Borromini A new Italian restaurant in Rittenhouse Square. A collaboration with Stephen Starr and Keith McNally WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Summer 2025 *photo credits: Jason Varney Testa Rossa To create a playful and sultry aesthetic, Fearless Restaurant group enlisted Stokes Architecture +Design. Using 1960s-inspired bold patterns and geometric prints positioned against Ferrari red moments, Stokes A+D gave the room a decidedly Italian maximalist allure. The centerpiece is a horseshoe-shaped pink marble bar-top, accompanied by round diner counter-style stools with green leather seats and triangular black-and-white printed backs. Bringing in more richness, brass shelving spans the backbar while high-gloss red finishes emulate from the soffit above. Opposite the bar, U-shaped booths in blue flame-stitch fabric are capped with silver pinecone-inspired table lamps and backed with a red-and-white mod-style screen divider. The striking Mutina Mattonelle Margherita tiled-flooring is a focal point of the bar area with bright colorways continuing the Italian superfluity motif. Custom upholstered banquettes, checker print tables, and scalloped chairs pop in vibrant colors orange, emerald, canary yellow, black, and white of throughout the room. To infuse a bit of everyday balance, Stokes A+D built in moments of natural wood on raised ceilings, incorporated marquetery at the base of the bar, and flanked the room with tambour paneled walls. Two types of terrazzo tiles are arranged as thick stripes across the dining room floors, leading the early 20th century Italian futurist design to the exterior with a circle-shaped breezeblock and scalloped lemon-colored umbrellas and rattan banquettes on the outdoor patio. WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Glen Mils, PA COMPLETED: Winter 2024 https://www.fearlessrestaurants.com/testarossa-glen-mills *photo credits: Jason Varney The Forth Hotel Stokes was asked to design the food and beverage concepts at the Forth Hotel in Atlanta. Elektra is a mediterranean-inspired restaurant and bar overlooking the pool deck. Jewel-toned fabrics, terrazzo, and a custom mural create a bold, breezy space for brunch, dinner, or drinks. Bar Premio is the hotel’s central bar and brings Italian café culture into a refined lobby setting. Marble, walnut, and soft lighting support a seamless shift from morning espresso to evening cocktails. Il premio is a modern Italian steakhouse with park views and rich interiors. Anchored by a wood-fired grill, the space unfolds into threedistinct dining roomsand a mural-wrapped bar lounge. Finally, Moonlight is a glamorous rooftop lounge nodding to 1970s Italian design. Alcantara upholstery, chrome, and backlit glass block set the stage for skyline views and retro-inspired cocktails. WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Atlanta, GA COMPLETED: Fall 2024 The Forth Hotel *photo credits: Matthew Williams Book Tower Stokes was asked to design the food and beverage concepts for several spaces in the Book Tower hotel in Detroit, MI. Le Supreme is a classic French brasserie with mosaic tile floors, antique brass, and a traditional zinc bar. Timeless and richly detailed, Le Supreme evokes Parisian café charm in a historic Detroit setting. Hiroki San is a moody, subterranean izakaya blending raw concrete with hand-crafted Japanese finishes. Featuring an open fire grill kitchen and tucked-away sushi bar, leading to the hidden cocktail lounge, The Aladdin Sane. The Aladdin Sane is a discreet cocktai

items.title: Meet — Stokes Architecture & Design
items.text: Meet — Stokes Architecture & Design Menu Wildwoods Welcome Signs Entering the town of Wildwood, the county wanted a welcoming entrance, and one that signals to visitors something about the town’s spirit. Stokes was hired to design a doo-wop sign that would be a compliment to our wildly popular boardwalk entrance sign LOCATION:Wildwood, NJ. COMPLETED:Summer 2020 Rio Grande Plaza Located at the end of the city’s primary east/west avenue, and bisecting the town’s primary beach parking location, Stokes Architecture aimed to create a new focal point for the town. The nine foot stainless steel letters of the sign are visible to all motorists entering the city via Rio Grande Ave., and the colorful use of stamped concrete and brick paving as well as the “beach ball” bollards invite pedestrians in a friendly, playful way to enter the boardwalk. The space also acts as a public transit stop, as visitors can take the vintage 1950’s tram car up and down the boardwalk. These planning strategies have paid off, as the plaza has become a busy gathering place, a great photo opportunity, and a contemporary icon for the town. LOCATION: Wildwood, NJ. COMPLETED: summer 2007 Tech Village Stokes was the architect and designer for the ground-up Tech Village at the Cape May County Airport. The project sits on a former WWII naval base and takes architectural cues from it's historic airplane hangar neighbors on campus.⁠ The exterior of the building is clad in composite board panels with vertical floor-to-ceiling windows weaved into the facade. The industrial styled space exposes its structure on the interior, with glulam beams creating the warm, arched ceilings. A second phase is currently being considered, with a Stokes-designed park/public open space between phases. WORK: -architecture -interior design LOCATION:Cape May, NJ COMPLETED:Spring 2020 *photo credits: Matt Wargo Stokes Architecture + Design Office After 14 years in our old office, Stokes finally upgraded our home locale, taking over the entire top floor of a 12-story deco building (built in 1939) which had been altered many times over the years. In its previous iteration, the whole floor had been divided into several individual offices and, most recently, painted purple. Stokes created an open floor plan, gutting the entire level and opening up the 360 degree views of the city to everyone. Work stations were arranged around the perimeter so that each employee has a window. Great care was taken to give employees several unique spaces to work away from their desks. The central core of the space contains the materials library with a large, central work top, as well as a work table and pin-up space adjacent to the office lounge and kitchen. Custom plywood furniture and wall panels were created by The Challenge Program using furniture grade birch plywood, cork tiles are strategically placed throughout the space to give impromptu pin-up space, and decor and furniture were selected to give a more comfortable, residential feel to the space in certain areas. Honeygrow Headquarters Honeygrow, the Philly-based fast casual food concept, wanted a headquarters and catering kitchen for their fast-growing company, and came to Stokes for the design. Located in a formerly abandoned, non-descript warehouse in Fishtown, the space is a mix of industrial and modern elements, playing up the factory setting. The existing factory sash windows were refurbished, and reused as glass partitions for the new executive offices. Skylights were added, with polycarbonate light funnels piping natural light into these offices, while simultaneously diffusing it into the open air desk area. The layout, a mix of traditional and modern office design, incorporates many elements of interest into work areas to create a friendlier and more open work environment. The open desk corral (with desks built by Delaware’s Challenge Program) is dotted with planters and a garden. The added mezzanine houses a quiet library, and lounge and leisure

items.title: Sip — Stokes Architecture & Design
items.text: Sip — Stokes Architecture & Design Menu Rival Bros. at The Rally A new cafe for Rival Bros. attached to the lobby at the Rally in Fishtown WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Fall 2025 www.rivalbros.com *photo credits: Jason Varney Rival Bros.: Jessup House A new cafe attached to the Jessup House Lobby in Midtown Village WORK: -architecture -interior design -custom furniture design -custom lighting design LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Winter 2024 www.rivalbros.com *photo credits: Jason Varney La Colombe: Manhattan Laundry Mixing the usual elements of a La Colombe café, Stokes blended old with new in the historic Manhattan Laundry building in DC. A wood counter, along with the existing brick walls, balances warmth against the colder steel panel walls. The existing structural steel was boxed out, and supplemented with new box beams to create a coherent architectural statement on the ceiling, and to give place to new lighting. LOCATION: Washington, D.C. COMPLETED: Fall 2016 WEBSITE: www.lacolombe.com/cafes *photo credits: Matt Wargo La Colombe: Bryn Mawr La Colombe’s first suburban location was built in a 90-year-old auto garage on a busy retail corridor. The café was designed to embrace the raw industrial aesthetic of the existing space, as well as the openness, while juxtaposing it with a few inserted classic café design elements. As such, there are large, garage-like gridded windows, and a roll-up vestibule overhead door to fit in naturally with the open, warehouse environment. As does the large super graphic “La Colombe” sign. In contrast, the long bar is dotted with classic globe lights, accented with brass trim, warm wood, and marble. LOCATION: Bryn Mawr, PA COMPLETED: Spring 2016 WEBSITE: www.lacolombe.com/cafes La Colombe: Fishtown La Colombe’s flagship store in the Fishtown section of Philadelphia, is the first café of its kind for the renowned coffee roasters. Located in a formerly abandoned warehouse and now housing (along with the café) a rum distillery, a full kitchen, bakery, tasting room, and the company headquarter’s offices, the challenge for Stokes Architecture was to maintain La Colombe’s artisanal café feel while remaining cognizant of the larger scale and additional program that this space required. Working loosely with the palette of the company’s existing coffee shops and being mindful of the industrial warehouse background, Stokes aimed to create a new composition of materials that felt sleek and traditional at the same time. Using custom built furniture and display units designed by Stokes, the space was divided visually into smaller parts, highlighted by different materials and construction methods (as well as a huge mural by renowned muralist ESPO). The primary focus of all of La Colombe’s cafes is the customer and their procession through the space; from ordering, to pick-up, to sitting down. This cycle of use determined the layout for the space, with a winding counter top that moves the customers deliberately through the space, and ample seating flanking it on 3 sides. This counter (and its wood grid ceiling) is one of two primary focal points in the space. The other, in the rear of the building, is a glass and steel box showcasing the brass distillery equipment. LOCATION: Philadelphia, PA COMPLETED: Fall 2014 WEBSITE: www.lacolombe.com/cafes La colombe: Independence Mall The strategy for the La Colombe at Independence Mall was to be as unobtrusive as possible, respecting the beauty of the Pietro Belluschi designed lobby inherited (part of the old Rohm and Haas Building in Philadelphia). The counter sits as an island, wrapping but not actually touching the shaped concrete column. The materials strike a balance between La Colombe and Belluschi, with wood slats to match the existing walls, and the steel panels and marble counters maintaining La Colombe's style. items.title: The Modern Tiffin — Melissa Hom Photography
items.text: The Modern Tiffin — Melissa Hom Photography 0 The Modern Tiffin “Traditionally, a tiffin is a two- or three-layered, stacked steel lunch box intended to separate each component of a meal. So you can have your rice or chapati in the first layer, a vegetable masala dish in the second, and a daal (stewed lentils) in the third layer. The concept helps retain the integrity of each dish and helps in maintaining how Indian food is traditionally eaten - each component separate, not mashed up together in a bowl.” Next Next Kodwari

items.title: Kodwari — Melissa Hom Photography
items.text: Kodwari — Melissa Hom Photography 0 Kodawari The word “kodawari” represents the artisan’s pursuit of perfection. This book, Kodawari by Washoku Rooms, follows the unique journeys of two acclaimed Japanese chefs—Mitsunori Isoda of Omakase Room by Mitsu, and Isao Yamada of Kaiseki Room by Yamada—whose careers celebrate historical Japanese cuisine. Each chef relocated from his home country to prove himself in New York, one of the world’s most rigorous and respected culinary capitals. Previous Previous The Modern Tiffin Next Next Harney & Sons Tea

items.title: Spaces — Melissa Hom Photography
items.text: Cornell Morrison Dining Hall “Cornell University already boasts prestigious and very highly rated hospitality, food science and agriculture schools, as well as a dining program that is a perennial presence in the Top 10 of the Princeton Review’s Best Campus Food listing and other college food rankings.So what can be added to up that already elevated game? How about Morrison Dining, a 58,230-sq.ft. food hall style complex with 11 micro restaurant concepts and, sitting in the middle of it, a 2,400-sq.ft. food lab that melds the school’s dining service and academic missions through a collaboration between Cornell Dining and the Division of Nutritional Science. That combination has earned Morrison the 2022 FM Best Concept Award in the Best New Facility category.” - Food Management Magazine

items.title: Services — Studio UNLTD
items.text: How we can help. Our Services Interior Design Full delivery of interior design from concept through construction administration is at the heart of what we do. We thrive on generating creative solutions that move our projects forward and create memorable spaces. By taking the time to deeply understand the vision of the client, we are able to execute our projects at the highest level. Lighting Design For us, the importance of lighting in maintaining the overall look and feel of a space cannot be overstated. We approach lighting design with great integrity, offering practical design solutions to create soulful and inspiring environments. Custom Furniture & Lighting Our strong relationships with trade artisans coupled with our experience in furniture design enable us to bring bespoke solutions to our projects. Procurement We offer a full suite of procurement services through specification, budgeting, purchasing, VE and installation. Feasibility, Programming & Thought Partnerships With years of experience in hospitality design, we offer comprehensive services to guide clients through every stage of their projects. From exploring potential solutions to defining project scope and creating a solid foundation for success, leverage our expertise to guide the way. We’d love to hear about your project and how we can help bring it to life. CONTACT US

items.title: Honda Center Encore — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Honda Center Encore Implemented incrementally through 2027, in preparation for the arena to serve as an event venue in the 2028 Summer Olympics, the redesign includes a complete refresh of all food and beverage spaces, including multiple new F&B concepts, and an all-inclusive club on the club-level, offering an upscale, hospitality-focused experience for premium guests, with curated food and beverage offerings. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Anaheim, CA YEAR On The Boards CLIENT OC Sports and Entertainment 15,000 sq. ft. interior SIZE The project includes the debut of new opera box suites on the main concourse and a full renovation of all 68 existing luxury suites to deliver an elevated, modernized premium experience. East Club (above) and West Club (below) are two of multiple clubs designed by Studio UNLTD under construction in 2026 for Honda Center Encore.

items.title: Sushi Nakazawa — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Sushi Nakazawa The diminutive interior of Sushi Nakazawa Los Angeles is inspired by an underwater cavern, where deep blues, shimmering golds, and dramatic light create a sense of wonder and exploration. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Beverly Hills, CA YEAR 2026 Daisuke Nakazawa & Alessandro Borgognone CLIENT 2,607 sq. ft. interior | 1,401 sq. ft. exterior SIZE The energetic focal point to the room, the sushi counter, is a pristine white quartz countertop with a slate veneer facing evocative of a sea cave wall. A curving, dark plaster ceiling of deepest marine blue is made more dramatic by long slots that allow shafts of light to cut through. Mural inspired by the ancient “suminigashi” Japanese marbling technique . The entry path is shrouded by a slatted plaster façade creating a “tunnel” which offers privacy from the street.

items.title: Picala — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Picala Located at the crossroads of a busy commuter corridor and the entrance to the new Cumulus mixed-use district, the design of Picala unfolds with a soft yet impactful ambiance that feels welcoming and warm while maintaining a strong visual connection to its urban location. Against this industrial backdrop, the design flows with a carefully composed residential sensibility and a calming color story inspired by the soft hues of natural pigments. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Los Angeles, CA YEAR CLIENT SIZE 4,679 sq. ft. interior | 1,000 sq. ft. exterior Acme Hospitality Group 2026 “ Incorporating a sculptural lighting element to emphasize the visibility of excitement and communicate a sense of warmth was central to Acme’s vision for the space . ” Becky Becheanu Lead Designer | Lighting Designer Glossy red tile detail lends a dynamic energy to counter seating at the expo kitchen. Custom furnishings marry supple leathers with textural woven fabrics for a homey, inviting feeling.

items.title: Fleurette — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Fleurette Located in the coastal enclave of La Jolla, California, the design of Fleurette captures the effortless sophistication of seaside living in a visual dialogue between the elements of land and sea. For inspiration, the design team drew from Chef Travis Swikard’s personal and culinary heritage linking him to the kindred regions of Southern California and the Cote d’Azur. The result is a joyful choreography of natural materials at play with pure color and sculptural forms. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION La Jolla, CA YEAR 2025 CLIENT Chef Travis Swikard 5,700 sq. ft. interior | 4,600 sq. ft. exterior SIZE “ Fleurette challenged us to create intimacy within a gestural and modern, three-sided glass building. The result is a space that balances elegance with comfort through a detail-rich layering of travertine, wood, sculptural forms, and light.” Greg Bleier Founding Principal A monolithic elliptical bar functions as an architectural centerpiece that anchors the space. Copper highlights and bar stools in rusty red lend nuance and a playful pop of color. A dynamic lighting element that spans the entire ceiling of the main dining room evokes the gentle motion of ship sails. As guests circulate through the space, layered moments continue to unfold. Paneling in varied wood tones lines the corridor to the private dining room, recalling the repetition of berth doors along a ship’s passageway, and a glass-enclosed red wine room recalls Parisian storefronts In the private dining room, twin walnut tables are illuminated by a custom chandelier of cascading glass-bead curtains.

items.title: Vaca — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Vaca Nestled on the ground level of a residential tower in downtown Los Angeles, the interior of Vaca softens and reshapes the existing space with forms evocative of a subterranean cavern. Sweeping, gestural curves are accentuated by layered lighting to guide the flow, creating an enveloping experience that offers an escape from the surrounding cityscape. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Los Angeles, CA 2025 3,909 sq. ft. interior | 1,062 sq. ft. exterior CLIENT Chef Amar Santana | Vaca Group YEAR SIZE In keeping with Chef Amar Santana’s dynamic spirit, every detail of Vaca is designed to connect guests with the conviviality and craft inherent in Spanish cuisine. Rough materials including a handmade Mexican Cotto tile in Zocalo shape add interest and depth. Deep saffron-colored tile wraps the kitchen walls, extending the warmth and vibrancy of the of the dining area into the back of house.

items.title: Cosetta — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Cosetta For the design of Cosetta, Studio UNLTD set out to create a space that fosters an exchange between the tranquility of nature and the architecture of the interior. Inspired by chef Zach Pollack’s culinary quest in the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy, the design interprets the aspirational lifestyle of the Italian kitchen garden through the lens of a forward-looking, modern aesthetic where the transition between indoors and out is softened, and materiality and forms are approachable yet elevated. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Santa Monica, CA YEAR CLIENT SIZE 2,400 sq. ft. interior | 2,650 sq. ft. exterior Chef Zach Pollack 2025 “ Chef Pollack had a very clear vision that the restaurant should seamlessly extend from the dining room out onto the patio .” Terri Robison Principal Repeating arches rise up the wall then vault over to delicately drop partially over the counter, punctuated at their truncated ends with glowing globes of light. End-view perspective in which the arches seem to repeat infinitely in back-painted glass. Loose and built-in seating areas are nestled between a network of curved Corten steel planters lush with greenery.

items.title: Helms Bakery — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Helms Bakery Within the historic site of the fabled Helms Bakery, which delivered its last bread in 1969, rises an adaptive reuse project undertaken by Studio UNLTD. The renovation of the 6,880 square foot bow-trussed former garage space brings to the Culver City Arts District a majestic market hall with soaring ceilings and abundant natural light. The studio employs a modern yet nostalgic design vernacular to reintroduce present-day Angelenos to the Helms brand whose identity is indelibly woven into the cultural fabric of the city. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Culver City, CA 2024 6,880 sq. ft. interior | 1,000 sq. ft. exterior CLIENT Chef Sang Yoon | WNM Realty YEAR SIZE “ We wanted to work in subtle hints of the building’s history without hammering in too much art deco. We did this by layering in touches of nostalgic and traditional design elements." ” Greg Bleier Founding Principal Historic details of the building are reproduced along the new façade that match the original 1930’s construction, and custom Art-Deco pendants add to the charm. Repeated iterations of custom Art-Deco inspired arched wood “storefronts” connect the design lexicon of the bakery to the adjacent dinette.

items.title: Sera — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Sera The design of Sera, Honolulu takes inspiration from the pristine bays of the Hawaiian Islands and the sculptural forms of the ko’a reefs that lie at the heart of a dynamic underwater landscape. Located on the ground floor of the Renaissance Honolulu Hotel and Spa, the interiors explore the interconnectedness between nature and man through materiality and forms inspired by local fishing traditions and craftsmanship. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Honolulu, HI YEAR 2024 CLIENT Marriott SIZE 6,700 sq. ft. “ Studio UNLTD delivers a design aesthetic that is dynamic, engaging and alluring. ” Patric Yumul, CEO Table One Hospitality Trio of Hollywood booths backed with an amorphous graphic print that’s visible to passersby on Kapiolani Boulevard. photography by Christopher Rohrer A bold mural wallcovering featuring graphic tropical foliage in mango orange, soft pink, chartreuse, and blues defines a unique seating nook. A large picture window framed in warm wood provides a view into the wine room to highlight the restaurant’s extensive wine program.

items.title: Cino — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Cino The interior of Cino, Honolulu is a striking convergence of maximalism, Art Deco and contemporary styles where saturated colors intermingle with plush florals, animal prints and crisp geometric shapes in unexpected ways to create a complex visual feast for the eyes. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Honolulu, HI YEAR 2023 CLIENT DB Restaurant Group SIZE 3,000 sq. ft. interior | 700 sq. ft. exterior The cocktail bar is flanked by a smaller raw bar which echoes its design features: ribbed teal-blue tile bar face, amazonite marble bar top, decorative brass shelving and slatted, baroque-inspired molding. Overhead, a hexagonal chandelier of polished brass set in a mirrored recessed cove casts an ambient glow. Twin curvilinear banquettes in sumptuous fabric whose palette of pinks, gold, chartreuse and claret is formed by an explosion of giant flower petals. In the spirit of an eccentric artist’s apartment, the restaurant interior is composed of three distinct areas: main cocktail bar and lounge at the entry, dedicated raw bar, and main dining room. Underfoot, marble-look black and white porcelain tiles laid out in an oversized diagonal chevron pattern visually link the three spaces. “ It was important to the client that the design be bold and transportive .” Terri Robison Principal Deep mulberry is the dominant color in the main dining room and serves as the backdrop for layers of flora and fauna prints, textured upholstery, and large chromatic portraits of exotic animals. Plush velvets surround, including an ultra-feminine floral print banquette and dining chairs in saturated Kelly-green velvet. Accents including polished brass and high-gloss tables tops layer in a touch of luxe glamour to complete the Avant Garde vibe.

items.title: Saizon — Studio UNLTD
items.text: Saizon The design for Saizon explores the tension between the opposing qualities of permanence, represented by architectural structure, and fluidity, symbolized by the perpetual ebb and flow of the ocean. Heavily plastered columns and beams, reminiscent of decaying concrete pier supports add a dramatic gridded framework to the room while board-formed concrete wall tiles provide texture and depth. Contrasting with the steadfastness of the “concrete” structure is a diverse array of materials and shapes strategically employed to create different rhythms in the room. PROJECT SUMMARY LOCATION Fresno, CA YEAR 2022 CLIENT Brandon Smittcamp SIZE 5,300 sq. ft. interior | 850 sq. ft. exterior “ Tertiary cities are often deprived of thoughtfully designed restaurants and the owners really wanted to make a bold statement. The feedback thus far has been incredible. ” Greg Bleier Founding Principal Striking color and energetic brush work of artist Yomar Augusto derives inspiration from the geometries of the space. Architectural lighting spotlighting the tables is layered with accent lighting that calls attention to the columns and beams, artwork and custom wall treatments. Custom armed pendants mounted along the spine of the double-sided banquette feature textured ceramic shades and leather strapping. A palette grounded in the earthy, natural colors of warm leathers, dark-stained oak, and various shades of black, is disrupted by moments of vibrant ocean blues and copper highlights.

items.title: THE SPRINGS - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: THE SPRINGS - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design THE SPRINGS Taichung, Taiwan Located in Taichung, Taiwan, The Spring is a high-end residential condominium developed by Pao Huei Property Development, conceived as a refined sanctuary shaped by proportion, materiality, and a strong relationship to the surrounding landscape. Tihany Design was commissioned to design all public interiors and amenity spaces, establishing a contemporary residential environment defined by calm, continuity, and understated elegance. Inspired by the project’s name, references to nature are woven throughout the interiors through a soft, nuanced palette, tactile surfaces, and custom details that foster a seamless connection between interior and garden. A vaulted ceiling traces the central axis of the six-meter-high lobby, evoking the sensation of walking beneath a canopy of trees and reinforcing a sense of serenity across the shared spaces. ___________________ RESIDENCE ___________________ CLIENT Pao Huei Development visit website﻿ Photo Amaury Laparra Previous AT.MOSPHERE Next THE PENROSE ROOM NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.title: THE PENROSE ROOM - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: THE PENROSE ROOM - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design THE PENROSE ROOM Colorado Springs, CO, United States Set within The Broadmoor in Colorado Springs, The Penrose Room reimagines one of America’s most storied dining destinations through a layered interior narrative shaped by legacy, landscape, and cultural exchange. Founded in 1918 by Spencer and Julie Penrose, the resort’s spirit of adventure and refined European influence informs a design approach that bridges Old World elegance with the mythology of the American West. Working in close dialogue with this heritage, Tihany Design conceived a sequence of richly detailed environments, from an intimate arrival foyer to a lounge inspired by the conviviality of the Western saloon, reinterpreted through warm wood tones, leather detailing, and curated objects from the Penroses’ global travels. At its core, three distinct dining rooms express themes of ambition and cosmopolitan sophistication through tactile metals, jewel-toned finishes, and sculptural lighting, transforming The Penrose Room into a contemporary stage for ritual and celebration. ___________________ RESTAURANT RESTAURANT BAR ___________________ CLIENT The Broadmoor visit website﻿ ___________________ OPERATOR The Broadmoor Photo Amaury Laparra Previous THE SPRINGS Next VICTORIA PLACE NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.title: SAUSKA TOKAJ WINERY - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: SAUSKA TOKAJ WINERY - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design SAUSKA WINERY OF TOKAJ Rátka, Hungary In the world of winemaking, the family-owned and operated Sauska Winery of Tokaj in northeast Hungary represents an extraordinary new construct of architectural and interior design innovation — a genre-breaking, state-of-the-art wine manufacturing plant built atop the rolling hills of one of the country’s UNESCO World Heritage sites. Opening in 2024 the avant garde structure was created by BORD Architectural Studio to be visually spectacular with an astonishing, ecologically communal presence in the terrain. Despite its size and scale, the brilliantly designed edifice magically blends into its surroundings. Working in close harmony with the extraordinary building and to arm its decisive connection with nature, Tihany Design created fresh, fluid and organic interiors using natural materials of local stone, wood and metal in celebration of the local landscape, to ensure unmistakable unity with the environment. ___________________ WINERY RESTAURANT BAR RETAIL ___________________ CLIENT Sauska Visit website Photo Marc Goodwin Architect BORD Architect Previous FOUR SEASONS DIFC Next ORO CIPRIANI NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.title: VICTORIA PLACE - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: VICTORIA PLACE - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design VICTORIA PLACE Honolulu, Hawaii, United States Victoria Place represents a seamless transition from Honolulu’s distinctly lush, urban environment into the serene, artfully curated interior landscape of the newest Ward Village offering. From the elegant, airy lobby to the uniquely intuitive public spaces and each contemporary residence, Victoria Place exudes a bespoke, inviting atmosphere featuring enticing natural materials, authentic Hawaiian design inspiration and the utmost attention to detail. The diverse, refined material palette creates a balanced composition of the elements; showcasing the harmony of rhythmic graphic symmetry and organic forms. The Victoria Place residences exude a sophisticated lightness with fresh pops of color and warm, thoughtful details that, together with breathtaking front-row views and the vibrant community philosophy of Ward Village, create a new standard of luxury living. ___________________ RESIDENCE ___________________ CLIENT The Howard Hughes Corporation visit website﻿ Photo cpurtesy of Howard Hughes Previous THE PENROSE ROOM Next PER SE NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.title: BOUCHON BISTRO - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: BOUCHON BISTRO - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design BOUCHON BISTRO Coral Gables, Miami The design continues to evoke the true essence of Chef Keller’s traditional French bistro, Bouchon, which first debuted in 1998. That vision is to bring the atmosphere of a French brasserie to America with all the fine details that look and feel as though one were in Paris. By incorporating timeless pieces and elements – velvet and polished brass fixtures, ornate bar and decorative floor tiles - into a contemporary, yet intimate, and inherently French environment. That authenticity remains paramount, keeping in mind the original “bouchon,” a particular style café that has existed in the Lyon province for centuries. ___________________ RESTAURANT CHEF Thomas Keller ___________________ CLIENT Thomas Keller ﻿Visit website Photo Adrian Gaut Previous THE BREAKERS Next MANDARIN ORIENTAL AL FAISALIAH NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.text: PER SE - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design PER SE New York, NY, United States Per Se restaurant is a complex design portrait of world-class chef Thomas Keller, reflecting his unique brand of hospitality. The latest renovation (2023), while honoring the sophisticated DNA of the original restaurant’s design and architecture, introduces a new color scheme, bespoke furniture and furnishings, and subtle architectural updates. The Private West Room has been completely redesigned to meet the latest standards in technology and comfort. TK’s vision of a “timeless classic” restaurant continues to inspire the new design. Classic modern design elements set the stage for this rare culinary experience. ___________________ RESTAURANT MICHELIN RATED CHEF THOMAS KELLER ___________________ CLIENT THOMAS KELLER Visit website 3D Rendering Tihany Design Previous VICTORIA PLACE Next DANIEL NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.title: DANIEL - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design
items.text: DANIEL - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design DANIEL New York, NY, United States This is the second time in 11 years that the Michelin-starred Chef has entrusted Tihany Design to reconceive his stage, dining room and bar. Signature elements begin with the Chef’s cue of a red carpet-style arrival to an exquisite, polished stainless steel-arched entrance, a deliberate extension of the existing neoclassical motif of the restaurant’s interiors. Three adjacent mirrored arches segue to the redesigned lounge area with custom furnishings, ombre red carpet, a color scheme of rich grays, and a spectacular crystal-enhanced, Art Deco-inspired bar designed in partnership with Lalique. The reflectivity of the space illuminates the dialogue between past and present, providing its rich history with a delightful path forward. ___________________ RESTAURANT Michelin Rated CHEF Daniel Boulud ___________________ CLIENT Daniel Boulud ﻿visit website﻿ Photo Eric Laignel Previous PER SE Next THE BREAKERS NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.text: THE BREAKERS - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design THE BREAKERS Palm Beach, FL, United States Tihany Design has gone on to breathe new life into a number of venues across the property in the ongoing renovation of the iconic Palm Beach resort. In addition to HMF, Tihany-designed spaces include The Lobby, The Flagler Steakhouse, Seafood Bar, Flagler Club Lounge, the South Oceanfront Tower guest rooms and suites and the specialty suites Royal Poinciana and Imperial. From dining venues to guest rooms, the new design maintains the integrity of the historic property while infusing each space with a renewed sense of Palm Beach sophistication and spirit. ___________________ HOTEL GUEST ROOMS & SUITES PUBLIC SPACES RESTAURANTS ___________________ CLIENT, OPERATOR The Breakers Palm Beach ﻿visit website﻿ Photo Eric Laignel; Riccardo Piazza Previous DANIEL Next BOUCHON BISTRO NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

items.text: MANDARIN ORIENTAL AL FAISALIAH - Tihany Design - Luxury Interior Design MANDARIN ORIENTAL AL FAISALIAH Riyadh, Saudi Arabia Located in the heart of Riyadh, the 5-star Al Faisaliah Hotel has been remastered and rebranded as the newest Mandarin Oriental property in the Middle East. Tihany Design led the redesign of all guest rooms and suites as well as the ground floor lobby, level 1 meeting rooms and 3 atriums. Guests arrive at a ground floor oasis, stepping onto natural stone flooring encircling a rich, blue-hued lobby and adjacent reception area. Mandarin Oriental Riyadh’s three atriums each feature a bespoke art piece, creating distinction between the four buildings of the hotel while further connecting the design to its unique location in the world. ___________________ HOTEL GUEST ROOMS & SUITES PUBLIC SPACES EVENT SPACES ___________________ CLIENT Al Khozama ___________________ OPERATOR Mandarin Oriental Visit website﻿ Photo Marc Goodwin Previous BOUCHON BISTRO Next MANDARIN ORIENTAL BOSPHORUS NEW YORK 135 West 27th Street New York, NY 10001 t. +1 212 366 5544 LEGAL privacy policy cookie policy copyright © Tihany Design

THE PRINCIPALS The woman-founded and led team behind Electric Bowery, established in 2013, is a collaborative group of architects, designers, and developers led by licensed architects and Design Principals, Lucia Bartholomew and Cayley Lambur. They guide their studio by blending their individual and joint experiences in both residential and hospitality projects, their entrepreneurial business sensibilities, into a truly defined design vision. Cayley & Lucia first met while working together at Gehry Partners in Los Angeles, and then went on to found Electric Bowery. In its beginnings the studio developed its portfolio through residential development, with the pivotal concept that good design holds value. Electric Bowery believes successful design projects should be both approachable and inspiring – there is no ‘one size fits all’. We are listeners, thinkers, and creators. We believe in site specificity, celebrating the landscape, collaborating with local trades, and we always put the utmost value on collaborating with our clients. THE DIRECTORS Stephanie Luk Creative Director Stephanie has led the creative direction on a wide-ranging variety of hospitality, residential, and retail projects across the United States and abroad. She brings her diverse experience and conceptually driven design process to the team, with an eye for detail and thoughtful brand partnerships, that set the holistic Electric Bowery experience apart. Her distinctive approach to design stems from her multicultural experiences, her penchant for thinking outside the box and her ability to find inspiration from all of her surroundings. Daniella Gohari Design Director Since joining Electrical Bowery in 2014, Daniella has led the design and completion of an extensive range of projects while maintaining an emphasis on custom residential homes. With her broad experience in architecture and construction as well as her faculty for interior design, her strength lay in her role as an interdisciplinary thinker, bridging the Architectural and Interior divisions of the studio to collaborate holistically from inception to completion. Her perspective is informed by a respect for the contextual environment and historical styles coupled with connections to nature and a play on materiality. HOTEL LUCILE HOTEL LUCILE Photography By: Chase Daniel Set within a reimagined 1931 Presbyterian church in Silver Lake, Hotel Lucile transforms a historic place of gathering into a 25 key boutique hotel with a bar, restaurant, rooftop garden, and pool. The project approaches the existing structure with a sense of reverence and reinvention, preserving its architectural integrity while introducing a new layer of social and cultural life. The design draws from the language of the church itself, informed by the spirit of Peggy Guggenheim, the consummate collector. Conceived as the European home of an eccentric, well traveled hostess, the hotel unfolds as a series of curated spaces where art, furnishings, and objects feel accumulated over time. Historic materials and finishes remain foundational, while contemporary interventions introduce warmth, intimacy, and a lived in sophistication. The lobby is marked by the building’s original monumental wood entry doors, opening into interiors where plasterwork, moulding, and stained glass have been carefully preserved. These elements establish a rich architectural backdrop that anchors the project in its past while allowing new insertions to feel both intentional and effortless. The experience is lively and layered, forming an energetic threshold between the city and the interior. Dark millwork and preserved detailing ground the space, while the stair becomes an animated moment of color, light, and art. A rotating, shoppable art program curated in collaboration with Rhett Baruch Gallery is integrated throughout, inviting guests to engage with the work as part of the hotel’s evolving narrative. At the heart of the hotel, the former sanctuary has been transformed into a restaurant and bar that retains the dramatic volume and proportions of the original church. Stained glass windows filter light across original wood floors, preserving the spatial hierarchy. The altar has been reimagined as a flexible private dining room, and the choir loft now serves as an intimate lounge. Each intervention honors the history of the space while adapting it for contemporary use. Original stained glass windows depict the lives of saints, casting a layered ambient glow across the space. Beneath them, low-slung custom furnishings and rich, saturated tones create a sensual, lounge-like atmosphere that contrasts with the building’s historic scale. The result is a dynamic social core that feels both reverent and indulgent, where past and present are held in constant dialogue. “Lively, singular, and stylish, public spaces would beckon neighborhood creatives and visitors alike.” – Architectural Digest Each room feels intimate and personal, shaped by proportion, light, and an understated approach to luxury. Arched openings, dark wood built-ins, and tailored upholstery nod to the hotel’s European design cues. Parquet wood floors and soft plaster walls provide a historical backdrop for curated artwork and objects that feel collected over time. “From the beginning, we thought about it as almost an exhibition space, with this European villa feel, like you’re coming into a gallerist’s home,” – Lucia The bathrooms are defined by a layered, tactile material palette. Console sinks feature marble countertops, brass legs, exposed plumbing, and wall mounted fittings that reference traditional washstands. Deep green glazed tile introduces saturated contrast, while custom mosaic floors extend throughout, adding intricacy and variation underfoot. RIDGE HOUSE RIDGE HOUSE Photography By: Chris Mottalini Perched along the cliffs of Big Sur overlooking the Pacific, Ridge House is a home shaped by a deep connection to landscape, craftsmanship, and materiality. Originally built in 1994 by longtime local builder Frank Pinney for Esalen practitioner Hugh Milne, the residence embraces the rugged beauty of its surroundings through locally sourced stone, handcrafted redwood detailing, and carefully framed views of the wilderness. Three decades later, the home entered a new chapter, where custom furnishings, collected artworks, and a palette of enduring natural materials reinforce the original spirit of the architecture while creating a warm and contemporary retreat rooted in place. Layered with art, textiles, and collected objects, the living room reflects a thoughtful balance of cultural heritage and contemporary craft. Textiles weave Indian traditions into the home’s material story, while artwork and sculptural pieces introduce moments of discovery throughout the space. Roya Ghadimi’s striking figures from Big Sur’s Hawthorne Gallery bring a sense scale accentuating the room’s floor to wall windows and connection to the rugged landscape beyond. The exterior architecture balances ruggedness with refinement, drawing from the material language of the surrounding landscape. Locally crafted wood detailing and darkened metal surfaces weather gracefully in the coastal climate, while the home’s distinctive circular windows frame quiet moments within the expansive panorama. Embedded into the hillside and softened by native plantings, the structure feels both sheltered and inseparable from its setting. At the heart of the home, the kitchen and dining area celebrate craft, materiality, and gathering. Locally sourced redwood defines the space, extending from the exposed structure overhead to the custom millwork below to create a warm architectural backdrop rooted in Big Sur. Against this rich palette, a monumental ceramic vessel by Tyler Goin anchors the island, while a Brutalist-inspired dining table developed in collaboration with Corey Joseph Designs lends a quiet sense of permanence. Layered with commissioned ceramics by Jordan McDonald and a curated collection of objects, the space reflects an enduring dialogue between artistry, utility, and daily life. Conceived as a threshold between home and landscape, the entry vestibule unfolds through warm wood surfaces, filtered light, and framed views of the canyon. A vintage Ari Lounge Chair and Ottoman by Arne Norell establish a quiet place for pause, while a custom cowhide rug crafted from Argentinian hides introduces texture and softness underfoot. Together, the elements create an intimate moment of arrival that reflects the home’s balance. In the powder room, a custom copper vanity brings reflective warmth to the dark green plaster. The pairing lends depth and a sense of permanence to this intimate space, offering a refined counterpoint to the more rustic elements found elsewhere in the home. Beneath the loft’s pitched wood ceilings, soft layers and organic fibers temper the scale of the room, creating an atmosphere that feels both grounded and serene. Studio Ford textiles, including a custom screen and quilted bedding, introduce richness and texture while complementing the room’s architectural geometry. A wool rug adds an earthy warmth and comfort underfoot. The bedroom balances openness with intimacy, offering a retreat that feels deeply connected. WINDSOR SQUARE WINDSOR SQUARE Photography By: Laure Joliet Set within Los Angeles’ historic Windsor Square in Hancock Park, this 1927 French Eclectic residence has been thoughtfully renovated to honor its architectural legacy while introducing a more atmospheric and intimate way of living. Conceived for a family with a deep appreciation for music, hospitality, and gathering, the home balances preservation with reinvention, where original detailing and newly layered interventions coexist with ease. Drawing from the spirit of 1930’s New Orleans jazz culture and the energy of French brasseries, the design unfolds as a series of richly expressive rooms that feel cinematic and deeply personal, grounded in history yet alive with warmth, rhythm, and ritual. On arrival, a bold, sculptural artwork draws the eye. The foyer unfolds around it, where a sweeping staircase rises with quiet drama, its ironwork and curvature set against harlequin flooring that evokes a distinctly 1920’s sense of elegance. Nearby, a powder room introduces a moment of contrast, where punchy, expressive wallcovering brings a sense of wit and boldness, signaling the home’s embrace of both refinement and play. The front sitting room is composed as a more intimate counterpoint, where warmth and material depth take precedence. A palette of rich woods, warm textiles, and aged brass creates a sense of quiet enclosure, while the dark, enveloping ceiling lowers the scale and draws focus inward. Seating is arranged to encourage conversation, anchored by a rounded wooden sofa and layered upholstery that reinforces the room’s grounded, tactile quality. Framed by historic windows and a marble fireplace, the room settles into a quieter more intimate atmosphere, suited to slower, more reflective moments. The great room serves as the social center of the home, where a sense of energy and atmosphere take hold. Anchored by a curved, Gatsby-inspired bar, the space draws from the rhythm and glamour of a bygone era, designed as much for gathering as it is for cocktails. Rich materiality, like steel and mirror detailing, create a backdrop that extends the room outward towards the cheery spirit of the garden. Layered and inviting, the space is calibrated for hosting, where music, conversation, and movement naturally unfold. The kitchen deepens the home’s palette, where deep green, high-gloss cabinetry sets a rich, enveloping space. Polished brass catches and reflects the light throughout, introducing a subtle note of glamour against veined stone surfaces. At the center, a rounded island grounds the space, while French doors open directly to the garden, allowing the room to shift easily between everyday use and lively evening gatherings. A concealed wine room quietly links the kitchen and dining room, introducing a moment of surprise within the sequence of spaces. High-gloss green millwork, harlequin flooring, and brass detailing create a rich, immersive atmosphere, where material and color are used with confidence and depth. Beyond, the dining room softens, centered around a rounded table that invites gathering within a more composed setting. Together, the sequence reinforces the home’s sense of discovery, where movement between spaces is layered, deliberate, and theatrical. The primary bedroom shifts into a serene, more relaxed mood. Soft light and warm tones settle into the space, while subtle architectural curves frame the bed, creating a sense of calm and ease. Just beyond, the dressing room deepens in tone, where textured wallcoverings and custom millwork create a space that feels both intimate and expressive.
